340.body: The local backend is the service. It owns IDs, validation, trash, history, recurrence expansion, search ranking, and activity aggregation, which are the same responsibilities the Django backend has. The UI keeps calling the same /api/v1 contract and only reads and renders responses. In folder mode no note, course, planner, profile, or settings data goes to the Notechondria server: every request through the app's HTTP client is answered in the page (2.8). The requests that still leave the page carry no folder data: the manual "Check for updates" handshake (2.8 rule 3); the browser's own loads of absolute https image URLs that a note body or an adopted profile already contains (F32); and the portal's startup image when the user set it to a remote URL, a per-device preference (frontend/portal_app/lib/components/custom_splash_overlay.dart:67-79, F63). Class (b) calls go straight to the named third party (GitHub, a calendar host). The service lives inside each app's page rather than in a separate process. Because it speaks the backend contract, the same router could later run in a localhost daemon or in the desktop build, with the UI pointed at it through the existing API base URL setting. Whether the owner meant such a separate process is open question Q1. This design does not open any network listener.

late final NotechondriaClient _client = widget.client ?? HttpNotechondriaClient(httpClient: _localFolder.httpClient); LocalFolderController.forApp takes the storage mode from LocalFolderBoot.snapshot (2.8). Without a snapshot (today's widget tests) or on a native build, the mode is browserOrCloud. NotechondriaApp gains LocalFolderController? localFolder, the app-level test seam. Folder smoke tests pass a controller built over MemoryFolderPlatform (8.2) and no client, so the production line above runs in tests and its inner http.Client() resolves to the test's recorder (8.5). _localFolder goes to AppShell(localFolder: ...) (editor :94, planner :82, portal _buildShell at :92-105) and to the portal's _NoteRoutePage(localFolder: ...) (:121). main.dart passes prepare: LocalFolderBoot.preload to runGuardedApp (2.8). Each app gets these lines in the phase that ships its option (2.10). Portal note route. _NoteRoutePage listens to the controller. In folder mode, while the folder state is needsPick, needsPermission, or error, it shows LocalFolderReconnectView instead of its error text. When the state becomes active and no note is shown, it calls _load() again (components/note_route_page.dart:33-53). A cold #/note/<uuid> start therefore renders the folder note once the folder opens, even when the user has to choose it again first. Multipart: replace request.send() with _httpClient.send(request) at the 8 sites in 2.1 (one line each), so uploads reach the transport and test clients. No base-URL override. The first draft set the base URL to https://local-folder.invalid/api/v1 in folder mode as a fail-closed backstop. That is dropped, because it could not hold: _loadInitialData, _applyLocalAppSettings, and _loadLocalState reset the base URL from _localSettings['api_base_url'] on every load (editor core/initial_data.dart:19-21, core/settings_helpers.dart:50-52, core/load_local_state.dart:56-58; planner :10, :39, :53; portal :10, :39, :50); applyAuthPayload runs both of the first two (app_shell_session_mixin.dart:301-316); and RFC 6761 only says resolvers SHOULD fail .invalid names, while an explicit HTTP proxy still receives the request. Routing by storage mode (2.8) ignores the host, so every updateBaseUrl caller can keep pointing the client at the saved cloud URL without effect. That saved URL is what the manual update check uses. Startup budget. HttpClientInternalsMixin.send (:120-124) applies the startup budget only to requests that the StorageModeClient sends to the network. It asks through a small LocalRoutingClient interface (routesLocally(method, uri)). Requests answered in the page are not network calls, so the frontend/AGENTS.md rule that startup network calls run inside the budget still holds. The transport bounds waiting for local requests itself (2.9), but not a disk that stalls inside a hold, so this exemption is required, not a convenience. pingBackend (ping_backend.dart:24-38) takes an optional http.Client. Its three callers pass only widget.apiBaseUrl, so today ping always calls top-level http.get: editor modules/settings_build.dart:326, planner modules/settings.dart:645, portal modules/settings.dart:475. Each _SettingsPage gains Future<PingResult> Function()? onPing, and the call becomes onPing: widget.onPing ?? () => pingBackend(widget.apiBaseUrl). The shell passes onPing: () => pingBackend(<api base>, client: widget.localFolder.httpClient) where it builds _SettingsPage(...). ping then goes through StorageModeClient: the local backend answers it in folder mode, and the network does otherwise, as today. Startup: a local_folder step, described in 2.9. In folder mode offline_mode is ignored and its switches are disabled (frontend/editor_app/lib/modules/settings_pages.dart:254-268, the shared AppPreferencesCard offlineMode parameter at frontend/notechondria_shared/lib/src/settings/app_preferences_card.dart:50-51) by passing onOfflineModeChanged: null (9.3). Offline mode would only stop local reads. _persistLocalCache is skipped in folder mode. 344.body:
The layout is a superset of the GitHub data-sync layout (backend/creators/services/github_sync.py:11-28, docs/integrations/github-sync.md:39-62), which already follows the portable-archive rule in docs/client/editor_app.md:14-18,50-53 (Markdown for prose, JSON/frontmatter for metadata, media as normal files; "local folder flows" are listed there as an adapter of the same shape). <chosen folder>/
├── manifest.json required; see 3.2
├── README.md written once at init; never parsed
├── profile/
│ ├── creator.json same keys as github_sync._profile_files (:116-158)
│ ├── settings.json {app_settings, app_settings_updated_at}
│ └── skill.md MCP skill text
├── courses/
│ └── <slug>.json one per course (github_sync._course_files :160-181, plus color_hue)
├── notes/
│ ├── <stem>.md YAML frontmatter + Markdown body
│ └── <stem>.meta.json sidecar: ids, metadata_json, custom_meta, client_draft_id, ...
├── history/
│ └── <note-uuid-hex>/
│ ├── index.json versions: id, reason, label, created_at
│ └── <version-id>.md snapshot body
├── planner/
│ ├── events.json planner events (shape of services.planner_event_payload :182)
│ ├── feeds.json calendar feeds without raw_ical
│ ├── feeds/<feed-id>.ics raw iCal of imported or last-fetched feeds
│ ├── sessions.json note study sessions
│ └── heatmap.json per-day activity counts
├── assets/
│ ├── avatar.<ext>
│ └── notes/<note-uuid-hex>/
│ ├── cover.<ext>
│ ├── attachments.json id, uuid, filename, content_type, size_bytes, created_at
│ └── attachments/<sanitized original filename>
├── recycle_bin.json pointer list, as in the GitHub layout
├── trash/
│ └── notes/<stem>.md + <stem>.meta.json (sidecar carries deleted_at)
└── .notechondria/ ├── index.json derived cache; safe to delete ├── import.json progress of an unfinished archive import (6.2 R4) └── journal/<op-id>.json write-ahead records for multi-file operations (3.4.1) <stem> is <note-uuid-hex> for notes the app creates, the same name github_sync._note_files uses (:184-242). Notes added by hand with any file name are adopted: the app writes a sidecar next to the file and never renames it. Two files that claim one UUID are handled in 3.7. Attachments keep their original (sanitized) file names so a user can find them in a file manager. The GitHub layout uses attachments/<attachment-uuid>.<ext> (github_sync.py:282-286); the GitHub push in folder mode maps names, and the backend restore script does not restore assets anyway (backend/scripts/github_sync_restore.py:21-24). Chrome's write swap files (<name>.crswap, 3.4) can appear next to any file while it is written. Nothing in the app reads, counts, exports, or deletes them. Debug logs and per-device preferences (theme, locale, API base URL, the portal startup image) stay in browser storage. They describe the device, not the data (decision D2, section 10). The folder settings handler drops these keys from every PATCH /settings/ and never returns them, so the reused settings push cannot write the cloud API URL into profile/settings.json (F08).
344.title: 3.1 Tree

345.body: manifest.json: {"format": "notechondria-folder", "layout_version": 1, "folder_id": "<uuid>", "created_at": "<RFC 3339>", "created_by_app_version": "0.1.NNN", "id_counters": {"course": 0, "note": 0, "version": 0, "session": 0, "event": 0, "feed": 0, "attachment": 0}, "github_sync_schema_version": 1}, plus restored_from_folder_id after a .nchron restore (3.3). Each counter holds the last ID issued; the rules are in 3.7. The app refuses a folder whose layout_version is newer than it supports: "Folder not opened: Shared.LocalFolder/scan — manifest.json layout_version 2 is newer than this build supports (1). Update the app." Note .md: frontmatter keys follow github_sync._note_files (title, uuid, course_slug, is_public, editor_mode, last_edit, date_created) using the same quoted-scalar subset it writes. On read, title, course_slug, is_public, and the body are authoritative, so a user can edit them in any editor. Other keys are regenerated on write. Custom meta is read from the sidecar only, because github_sync spreads custom keys into the frontmatter after the system keys (:200-209) and a custom key could shadow a system key. Note .meta.json: schema_version, id, uuid, sharing_id, metadata_json, custom_meta, client_draft_id, note_type, source_note_uuid, cover_image_url (the sidecar fields of github_sync.py:224-241), plus description, word_count, and the md_size and md_last_modified seen at the last write (used in 3.8). planner/events.json and planner/feeds.json records may carry client_local_id, the browser-local ID they were pushed from (7.1). Every JSON file carries schema_version: 1, as github_sync does. Markdown links to attachments are stored on disk as relative paths (../assets/notes/<hex>/attachments/<name>), so the file renders in ordinary Markdown viewers. The note codec rewrites them to the nc-folder: scheme on read and back on write (3.6).

346.body: The v1 archive is a dump of _LocalAppStore buckets (docs/export_format_v1.md:8-29; writer frontend/notechondria_shared/lib/src/utils/local_archive.dart:135-246). The folder is shaped like the server data instead. Two rules make them interchangeable: Folder to .nchron. The export writes the normal v1 bucket files, derived from the folder (drafts.json holds every live note as a local draft with client_draft_id = fld_<uuid-hex>, courses.json the courses, planner_events.json and calendar_feeds.json the planner data, attachments/<client-id>/<file> the bytes). It also adds an optional folder/ subtree with a verbatim copy of the folder, minus .notechondria/ and *.crswap. readLocalArchive builds a name map and looks up only known entries (local_archive.dart:273-275), so v1 readers ignore folder/, and docs/export_format_v1.md:39-43 allows extra optional files without a version bump (decision D3). The copy repeats attachment bytes that the v1 attachments/ entries already hold, so attachment-heavy archives are about twice as large. .nchron to folder. If folder/ is present, restore it verbatim into an empty folder (lossless round trip), with one exception: the restore writes a new folder_id and keeps the original as restored_from_folder_id. A restored folder therefore never shares a lock name or a remembered-handle key with its source (3.7). Otherwise map buckets to records the way the post-login push does (section 7.1). Either way the import runs in chunks and writes manifest.json last (6.2 R4). So folder, zip, folder is lossless; browser-local, zip, folder keeps everything browser-local mode has; folder, zip, browser-local keeps notes, courses, and planner data but drops history and sessions, which browser-local mode does not model. Attachments on that last path are U16: the base64-to-LocalAttachmentStore move runs once per browser (frontend/editor_app/lib/core/local_persist.dart:51-55), so imported bytes may stay in the localStorage drafts bucket. Because the folder is a superset of the GitHub data-sync layout, a cloned data-sync repository can be opened as a folder (Phase 4 "adopt" action, ID rules in 3.7), and the folder can be pushed to GitHub with the same layout (feature F49). Two doc-versus-code differences in docs/export_format_v1.md should be fixed when the bridge lands: the collision suffix is __$i in code (local_archive.dart:179) but -<index> in the doc (:96), and the doc says import first wipes local state (:151-152) while the editor import only replaces six buckets (frontend/editor_app/lib/core/local_archive_io.dart:178-200).

349.body: Credentials are never written to the folder, to a .nchron export, or to logs. The folder may sit in a cloud-synced directory, and an archive is a file users share. local_archive.dart strips nothing itself; its comment makes stripping the caller's job (local_archive.dart:67-68). The folder bridge (9.2) applies a key denylist to every JSON object it exports (the v1 buckets and the folder/ copy), to the GitHub push, and to every write under profile/. Matching rule: keys are compared case-insensitively as whole keys, never as substrings. Stripped: the exact keys token, pat, secret, password, passphrase, authorization, cookie, credential, credentials, api_key, and apikey, and any key ending in _token, _secret, _password, or _key. The suffixes cover access_token, refresh_token, github_token, client_secret, and private_key. Exempt: path and any key ending in _path. .nchron attachment pointers use path (local_archive.dart:350-355), and app data also uses source_path and git_path. Test, both directions: a fixture with every key the bridge writes today plus the stripped list, nested at several depths. Every stripped key must be gone, and path, source_path, git_path, patch, pattern, tokens_used, and keyboard_layout must survive. A new benign key that ends in _key fails the test and must be added to an explicit exempt list. The only (b) features that need a credential are F49, F51, and F52, which use a GitHub fine-grained personal access token. F32 and F42 need none. F55 does not exist; a future LLM key would use the same store. How the user supplies it: in folder mode the GitHub card shows a token field and a link to GitHub's fine-grained token page, with the scope the App uses today (one repository, Contents read and write, Metadata read; docs/integrations/github-sync.md:33-37). The token is checked with one GET https://api.github.com/user before it is kept. Log lines name the outcome and never the token, its prefix, or its length: "GitHub token stored for this session: Shared.LocalFolder.GitHub/token — GET https://api.github.com/user accepted it as ''; it is kept in memory only." (or "remembered on this browser" with the opt-in) "GitHub token not stored: Shared.LocalFolder.GitHub/token — GET https://api.github.com/user answered ." "GitHub push unavailable: Shared.LocalFolder.GitHub/token — no fine-grained token is set for this session; paste one in the GitHub card." Where it lives (owner decision Q6): Option Exposure Cost Memory only (recommended default) Gone on reload; reachable by same-origin script only while the page runs Re-enter once per session "Remember on this browser": IndexedDB record through Shared.Credentials Readable by any same-origin page (6.1), the same exposure today's cloud session token has in localStorage (frontend/editor_app/lib/core/local_store.dart:275-285) None Remembered and encrypted with a passphrase (WebCrypto PBKDF2 and AES-GCM) Protects the stored copy at rest; does not stop a same-origin script that hooks the running page Passphrase prompt each session Desktop build with an OS keychain plugin Outside the browser Only with Q11

355.body: Each has a recommended default that the design assumes until answered. # Question Recommended default Q1 Did "dashboard for local services" mean a separate local service process (a localhost daemon) rather than an in-page backend? In-page backend (this design). The router speaks /api/v1, so a daemon or the desktop build can host it later; no network listener now Q2 Chrome on Android has had the File System Access API since 132 (BCD; Chrome Q1 2025 post). Keep mobile excluded? Exclude in v1; Android picker and permission behavior is untested (U14) and FileSystemObserver is desktop-only Q3 On *.github.io, persist the folder handle in IndexedDB? Session only, with an unchecked "Remember this folder" opt-in and the warning in 6.1. Cost: each app asks for the folder once per page load, through "Choose '' again" (2.9) Q4 Serve the apps from a dedicated origin (custom domain for the Notechondria Pages site)? Recommended; needs DNS and a base-href change in frontend-pages.yml, so it is a separate round. It removes the other Pages projects from the origin; uploaded /media/ files share an origin only where the app and the backend do, as on the loopback preview and the self-host (6.1, Q19) Q5 One folder shared by editor, planner, and portal, with an app's live cloud session taking precedence over it (2.10)? Shared; a live cloud session wins and the app shows the notice Q6 Where do credentials for (b) features live? Memory only, opt-in "remember on this browser" (section 5) Q7 Is a user-supplied fine-grained token acceptable for GitHub in folder mode? Yes; the GitHub App flow stays cloud-only (F50) Q8 Add an anonymous backend proxy for calendar URLs without CORS? No; it reintroduces the server and an open fetch proxy. Use file import Q9 Version banner in folder mode? Hidden; a manual "Check for updates" in the status card sends one unauthenticated GET /handshake/ to the saved cloud URL (2.8 rule 3) Q11 Folder mode for the native desktop build through dart:io (it would also fetch calendar URLs without CORS)? Follow-up after v1; until then the option is hidden on native builds (1.3) Q12 Full-fidelity "move folder to cloud"? Follow-up; interim paths in 7.3 Q13 Add a CI step that fails if the OPFS test-hook marker is in a release bundle, and a Chrome-platform test job? Add the grep guard. No Chrome job: OPFS tests run in the Playwright/Chromium container on a host with at least 16 GB RAM (8.3) Q14 Add a backend test that checks the contract fixtures against the live serializers? Yes, in Phase 1: it fails on a key or JSON-type difference and uploads the live responses as a CI artifact, so fixtures can be refreshed without a local backend (8.4) Q17 The apps call GET /auth/session/ and POST /auth/logout/, which the backend does not route (backend/notechondria/api_urls.py:64-136). Intended? Out of scope here; the folder backend answers both. Track separately Q18 Connecting moves this browser's drafts into the 30-day local recycle bin and its pushed planner items into a 30-day recovery list (7.1). Keep, or leave browser copies visible? Keep the moves; visible copies would show every pushed portal event twice (frontend/portal_app/lib/core/build_page.dart:97) Q19 On origins that serve both the apps and backend /media/ (the loopback preview, the Docker self-host), serve uploads so they cannot run as same-origin pages (another host, Content-Disposition: attachment, or Content-Security-Policy: sandbox)? Track as separate backend hardening; it also protects the cloud session token the editor and portal keep in localStorage today (6.1)

360.body: Storage mode is per app: browserOrCloud (today's behavior) or folder. It is decided once per start, synchronously, before the root widget is built and therefore before any request: runGuardedApp gains an optional Future<void> Function()? prepare, awaited inside its zone after WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized() and before launch() (frontend/notechondria_shared/lib/src/startup/startup_guard.dart:35-39). Each wired app's main passes prepare: LocalFolderBoot.preload, which awaits SharedPreferences.getInstance() once and stores LocalFolderBoot.snapshot. That call loads every value into a cache (shared_preferences 2.5.4 shared_preferences_legacy.dart:79-96), and later reads such as getString are synchronous (:129), so the later _LocalAppStore calls reuse the same instance at no extra cost. LocalFolderController.forApp(app) (2.7) calls decideStorageMode, which returns folder only when the build is web, the shared key notechondria.shared.storage_mode (2.10) holds "mode": "folder", and the app has no saved cloud session. A saved session is read exactly as the app's loadSession reads it, a value that decodes to a map with a non-null token: editor: notechondria.editor.session, or, when that key is absent, the legacy notechondria.session that _migrateLegacyKeys would copy into it (frontend/editor_app/lib/core/local_store.dart:50-72, :287-299); portal: notechondria.portal.session (frontend/portal_app/lib/core/local_store.dart:76); planner: none, because it keeps its session in memory only (frontend/planner_app/lib/core/initial_data.dart:259-260). With a saved session the mode is browserOrCloud and 2.10 rule 2 applies. An app without the wiring (2.10 rule 1) has no controller and keeps today's behavior. preload catches its own errors. If browser storage cannot be read, the snapshot is empty, the mode is browserOrCloud, and the app logs "Local folder not checked: .Startup/local_folder — browser storage could not be read (); starting in browser-local or cloud mode." In folder mode the folder state starts as opening, and the local_folder step (2.9) opens the folder. After that the mode changes only on Connect and Disconnect; "Switch to this folder" (2.9) changes the folder, not the mode. The folder state (opening, needsPick, needsPermission, scanning, active, error, disconnected) never changes routing. StorageModeClient.send applies four rules: Mode browserOrCloud: forward to the inner http.Client, unchanged. Mode folder: hand every request to LocalFolderTransport, whatever its host, scheme, or path, except the single passthrough in rule 3. The transport finds the /api/v1/ segments in the path (a base URL may carry a prefix, for example https://host/notechondria/api/v1) and dispatches the rest. A path without them gets a 404 with "Request not answered: Shared.LocalFolder.Backend/route — is not an /api/v1 route, and folder mode sends nothing to the network." The one passthrough , for the manual "Check for updates" button in the status card (Q9). A request goes to the inner client only when all of these hold: it was issued inside runCloudVersionCheck(apiBaseUrl, ...), a zone value that only that button's onPressed sets (the zone mechanism of runWithStartupBudget, startup_budget.dart:105-127); the value is the saved api_base_url the checks below compare with, because the transport does not read the app's settings; the method is GET, with no body and no query string; the path ends with /api/v1/handshake/; the scheme is https, or http with a loopback host; the scheme, host, port, and path prefix equal the saved api_base_url. The client rebuilds the request with only Accept: application/json, dropping Authorization and every other header. Cookies depend on the API base: package:http 1.6.0's BrowserClient.withCredentials defaults to false (browser_client.dart:59), which maps to fetch credentials: 'same-origin' (:88). A cross-origin API base, such as the Pages deployment's default, therefore gets no cookies. A same-origin base, which is the default on localhost and 127.0.0.1 (editor core/helpers.dart:142-156) and so includes the loopback preview, may get the origin's cookies. They carry no authority there: the handshake is a public GET view (backend/notechondria/api_views.py:252-253), and the API authenticates only by Authorization header (ApiKeyAuthentication, CasdoorJWTAuthentication, TokenAuthentication, no session authentication, backend/notechondria/settings.py:287-304). The existing 8 s handshake timeout applies outside startup (frontend/editor_app/lib/core/http_client.dart:62-68). The response is read only for version and min_frontend_version. Any other request made inside that zone still goes to the transport. Log: "Cloud version checked: Shared.LocalFolder/version_check — GET /api/v1/handshake/ answered 0.1.NNN; no account data was sent." The automatic version polls (editor core/settings_helpers.dart:120-139) are not in that zone, so the local handshake answers them with the running build's version and the banner stays hidden (F46). Folder states. The transport answers GET /handshake/ and GET /ping/ from memory in every state. In opening it holds every other request until the state changes, within the request's deadline (2.9), and then applies this rule for the state reached. A cold portal #/note/<uuid> start, whose _NoteRoutePage loads in initState (frontend/portal_app/lib/components/note_route_page.dart:33-44), and the guest public-notes fetch of a cold #/notes start (frontend/portal_app/lib/modules/learner.dart:98-110) are held this way and answered from the folder. Outside active the transport answers every other route, the (b) routes included, with 503 and a 1.8 detail: needsPick: "Folder not open: Shared.LocalFolder/restore_handle — this browser keeps access to '' for one page load only (session-only mode), so it has to be chosen again. Click Choose '' again." With "Remember this folder" on and the IndexedDB record missing (T3): "Folder not open: Shared.LocalFolder/restore_handle — this browser was set to remember '', but its saved folder handle is missing (browser site data was cleared, or the handle was never stored), so it has to be chosen again. Click Choose '' again." needsPermission: "Folder access lost: Shared.LocalFolder/permission — the browser no longer grants read and write access to '' (NotAllowedError, or access revoked while the tab was in the background). Click Reconnect." scanning: "Folder not ready: Shared.LocalFolder/scan — '' is still being indexed ( of entries). Try again in a moment." error: "Folder unavailable: Shared.LocalFolder/ — ." with the process and cause of the error that set the state. disconnected (another tab disconnected the folder, 2.10): "Folder disconnected: Shared.LocalFolder/disconnect — '' was disconnected in another tab. Reload to continue in browser-local mode." When another tab switched folders (2.9), the detail is "Folder switched in another tab: Shared.LocalFolder/connect — this browser now uses '' instead of ''. Reload to open it." All three apps keep a failed note save as a browser-local draft (editor core/note_crud.dart:136-160, planner core/note_crud.dart:139-158, portal core/note_crud.dart:135-150), and Reconnect pushes those drafts into the folder through applyAuthPayload (app_shell_session_mixin.dart:326-327). needsPermission is a routine state, not an edge case: Chrome revokes access for a tab that has been in the background for a while (1.4), so a user who switches away and back meets rule 4 regularly. Outside the app client, only the requests named in 2.6 leave the page. The smoke check "revoked mid-session" in 8.5 asserts that the test's recorder, which stands in for every http.Client(), receives zero requests in every non-active state.

361.body: The new local_folder step runs after local_state and before config and the handshake (editor frontend/editor_app/lib/core/bootstrap.dart:37-51, planner frontend/planner_app/lib/core/bootstrap.dart:37-54, portal frontend/portal_app/lib/core/bootstrap.dart:35-50). It makes no network request. The storage mode is already decided (2.8). In browserOrCloud mode the step returns at once and startup is unchanged. In folder mode the folder state is opening. Restore the handle. With "Remember this folder" on, it comes from the IndexedDB record (6.2), and the step calls queryPermission({mode: 'readwrite'}). In session-only mode, the default on *.github.io (Q3), the handle lives only in page memory, so after every reload and in every newly opened app tab there is none and the step goes to step 4b. A missing record in remembered mode is treated the same way. granted: read manifest.json, roll forward leftover journals under the exclusive lock (3.4.1), and load .notechondria/index.json. When the index exists and matches the layout version, the controller is active at once, and a verification rescan (3.8) runs after the startup pass, outside the budget zone; if anything changed, the UI refreshes through the change path (6.2). Note overwrites stay safe meanwhile, because every write re-checks the file on disk (3.8). Without a usable index the step scans in place (state scanning) and reports progress at least every 2 s on the splash status ("Reading folder '': 1,200 of 5,000 entries"). The step then calls applyAuthPayload with the local payload, as session_restore does for a saved cloud session (frontend/editor_app/lib/core/auth_flows.dart:168-177). The folder is pending. The step completes without waiting for a click, in either case below. The pass continues with the folder pending: the handshake is answered locally (2.8 rule 4), and session_restore, oauth_callback, and initial_data are skipped. The pass ends with the splash hidden and LocalFolderReconnectView shown in place of the shell (6.3); held requests get the 503 of the new state. a. prompt on a restored handle (expired or auto-revoked grant): the state is needsPermission, and the view offers "Reconnect ''". b. No handle: the state is needsPick, and the view offers "Choose '' again". denied, NotFoundError, or a newer layout_version: the controller enters error, and the reconnect view shows the matching message from 6.3 or 3.2. For denied and NotFoundError it also offers "Choose '' again". In folder mode, session_restore is skipped, because the folder session comes from step 3. oauth_callback is skipped too; a leftover ?code= logs "Sign-in not completed: .Startup/oauth_callback — this app is in folder mode; disconnect the folder to sign in to the cloud." config logs "API base resolved: .Startup/config — folder mode; requests are answered in the page (the saved URL is used only by Check for updates)." Splash. The 12 s force-hide (kBackendStartupTimeout + 2s, editor core/bootstrap.dart:25-32, planner :26-27, portal :24-25) stays as the safety net. Each progress report from the step re-arms it for another 12 s, so a long first scan keeps its progress visible. If the step reports nothing for 12 s, the timer hides the splash as it does today. Reconnect (a handle exists). The "Reconnect ''" button calls requestPermission({mode: 'readwrite'}) first in its onPressed (1.3). On granted it runs step 3, including applyAuthPayload. That runs in the gesture's zone, outside any startup budget (runWithStartupBudget is zone-scoped, startup_budget.dart:105-127), so a slow folder cannot trip the budget or make later requests skip as "Cloud data not loaded". A mid-session reconnect uses the same path; the handle is still in page memory then, in session-only mode too. Choose again (no handle). The "Choose '' again" button calls showDirectoryPicker({id: 'notechondria-folder', mode: 'readwrite'}) before any await in its onPressed (1.3). The fixed id makes the picker open where it was last used with that id (MDN). The picker includes Chrome's grant for readwrite; when the user closes it or declines the grant it throws AbortError (MDN). Only after it returns does the app read the picked folder's manifest.json, in the same gesture zone and outside any startup budget: Same folder_id as the shared key: the copy check of 3.7 runs, the handle is kept in page memory (and in IndexedDB when "Remember this folder" is on), and step 3 runs, including applyAuthPayload. No manifest.json (an empty folder, or any folder that is not a Notechondria folder): the app writes nothing to it and shows "Folder not opened: Shared.LocalFolder/pick — '' has no manifest.json, so it is not ''. Choose '', or use browser-local mode and connect a new folder from the sign-in screen." Starting a new folder is a separate, explicit Connect, so a mis-click cannot make the data look lost. A different folder_id (another Notechondria folder): refused by default with "Folder not opened: Shared.LocalFolder/pick — '' is a different Notechondria folder (folder_id <8 hex>) from '' (<8 hex>), which this browser uses. Choose '', or switch this browser to ''." The message comes with a "Switch to this folder" button. Switching: writes the shared key with the new folder_id, folder_name, connected_by, and connected_at; deletes the old folder's remembered-handle record and, with "Remember this folder" on, stores the new one; posts {op: "switch", folder_id} on the change channel (6.2). Other tabs in folder mode enter disconnected with the switch detail of 2.8 rule 4; tabs in browser-local mode show the connect banner of 2.10 rule 5; runs step 3, and then the push of 2.10 rule 3, because this is the app's first start in that folder. A newer layout_version: the 3.2 message. AbortError: the view stays as it was, and the app logs at INFO "Folder not chosen: Shared.LocalFolder/pick — the picker closed without a folder (AbortError)." Cost. In session-only mode each app asks once per page load: after every reload and in every newly opened app tab, because v1 passes no handle between tabs (6.2). With "Remember this folder" on, a restored handle takes the Reconnect path instead. A second app tab then usually needs no prompt at all while another tab of the origin holds the grant, because the grant belongs to the origin (6.1). Bounds. Local requests do not use the startup budget (2.7). The transport also bounds each request, measured from the moment LocalFolderTransport.send receives it: Every lock wait is at most 5 s (6.2 R5) and never longer than the time left before the request's deadline. Each wait gets its own AbortSignal.timeout(min(5 s, time left)). Read deadline: 8 s for a GET. It covers the hold in opening (2.8 rule 4), every lock wait (the shared lock and, on the R3 path, the exclusive lock for roll-forward and the shared lock again), the roll-forward itself, and the handler. At the deadline the GET answers 503 with "Folder data not loaded: Shared.LocalFolder.Backend/route — GET took more than 8 s ()." The cause is "folder still opening", "waiting for the folder lock", or "folder reads stalled". Write deadline: 7 s for a write to start, that is, to write its journal record (3.4.1 step 2) or, for a single-file write, to open the writable. It covers the same waits as a read. A write that misses it has changed nothing and answers 503 with "Change not saved: Shared.LocalFolder.Backend/route — could not start within 7 s ()." All three apps keep such a failed save as a browser-local draft (2.8). A write that has started runs to the end, because stopping it would only leave work for roll-forward. R4 caps that hold at a 2 s target and 50 file writes, so a write normally answers within about 9 s. These deadlines bound waiting. They do not bound a disk that stalls inside a hold, for example a close() that never returns. That is why the startup-budget exemption in 2.7 is still needed: the deadlines alone do not keep every local request under the 10 s budget. Wording. In folder mode the later steps use folder wording. The handshake step's splash label reads "Opening folder backend" instead of "Connecting to server". The initial_data step's label reads "Reading folder ''", and its failure consequence is "Folder data not loaded" instead of "Cloud data not loaded" (editor core/bootstrap.dart:89-96, and the matching planner and portal steps). _initialDataOutcome says "every folder request answered" instead of "every cloud request answered" (editor core/bootstrap.dart:182-196, planner :171-185, portal :173-187).

362.body: The connection is recorded once per browser in notechondria.shared.storage_mode, in shared_preferences, which on web is origin-wide localStorage: {"mode": "folder", "folder_id", "folder_name", "connected_by", "connected_at", "remember"}. remember is the "Remember this folder" choice (T3, StorageModeRecord); its default, rememberDefaultForOrigin, is off on every origin known today, because the 6.1 residual risk applies on *.github.io, the loopback preview, and any self-host, and an origin cannot show that it serves no uploads. A record without the key reads as off. Sessions are per app (notechondria.<app>.*; editor core/local_store.dart:33-47 explains the prefixes). The editor and the portal persist their cloud session (:275-285); the planner keeps it in memory only (frontend/planner_app/lib/core/initial_data.dart:259-260). Per-phase opt-in. An app honors the key only from the phase that ships its own option (9.1): the editor from Phase 2, the planner and portal from Phase 3. Before that the app has no local_folder step and ignores the key, so it never calls folder routes its phase lacks. A live cloud session wins. If the app holds a saved cloud session at startup (editor, portal), decideStorageMode returns browserOrCloud (2.8) and the app restores that session as today. It shows once per start, and the status card repeats: "Local folder not used: .Startup/local_folder — this app is signed in to the Notechondria cloud as '', which takes precedence over the folder '' connected on this browser. Sign out here to use the folder." If session_restore then clears the session, the signed-out AuthHub offers "Use the connected folder ''" (1.3). Otherwise the app uses the folder. On its first start in a given folder, the app pushes its own browser-local data in (7.1) and records notechondria.<app>.folder_pushed = <folder_id>. Disconnect never ends a cloud session. Disconnect calls disconnectFolder(), not logout(). Its steps run in this order, so that no request carrying Token local-folder can reach the inner client: The folder state becomes disconnected. Routing stays in folder mode, so a request already queued or still issued (a pending autosave, for example) gets a 503, here with "Change not saved: Shared.LocalFolder/disconnect — '' was disconnected in this tab; the change stays in this browser.", and the app keeps a failed save as a browser-local draft. The app clears its in-memory folder token and profile. A save that fires after this finds no token and takes the signed-out path. The app clears the shared key and the remembered-handle record and posts {op: "disconnect"} on the change channel (6.2). Only then does the storage mode switch to browserOrCloud, and the app reloads browser-local data. It never calls authClient.logout, never calls clearPersistedSession(), and never touches another app's keys. A folder-mode app has no cloud session of its own (rule 2), so nothing is lost. What a running tab shows when another tab changes the connection: this tab in browser-local mode, folder connected elsewhere: a banner "Folder connected in another tab: Shared.LocalFolder/connect — '' is now this browser's storage. Reload to use it; this tab's browser-local data will be copied in." this tab in folder mode, folder disconnected elsewhere: the folder state becomes disconnected, requests answer 503 (2.8 rule 4), and a banner shows that message. this tab in folder mode, another tab chose "Switch to this folder" (2.9): the same, with the switch detail of 2.8 rule 4. this tab holds a cloud session: nothing changes except the status card line from rule 2. in Phase 2 the planner and portal do not read the key and keep their own browser-local or cloud data. The editor's status card says "Folder used by the editor only: Shared.LocalFolder/connect — the planner and portal do not support folder mode in this release and keep their own data." The smoke checks in 8.5 cover rules 2 and 4, including the order in rule 4.

364.body: These steps run on the first connect and on the first start of each other app in that folder (2.10 rule 3), so each app moves its own browser-local data once per folder. First connect only: the folder is picked, the manifest written or validated, and the index built. Courses first. Before this step the app sets its in-memory token to local-folder, with no profile and no persistSession, because each app's _syncLocalCourse throws "Local course not synced" without a token (editor core/local_course_builders.dart:75-76, planner :94-101, portal :102-103). Step 4's applyAuthPayload then sets the same token together with the profile. The app pushes its browser-local courses through the app client with the local token, reusing its _syncLocalCourse (planner frontend/planner_app/lib/core/local_course_builders.dart:92-138; loop in core/maintenance_actions.dart:91-115). Each push upserts on client_course_id (3.7) and returns the folder course; _syncLocalCourse already remaps drafts to it (:107-115) and moves the local course into the browser-local recycle bin (:120). The step records local course id → folder course id for step 3. Events and feeds (planner and portal). These are is_local_event events (planner frontend/planner_app/lib/core/planner_builders.dart:5-29), is_local_feed feeds (frontend/planner_app/lib/core/local_calendar.dart:34), and portal events with local-<micros> IDs (frontend/portal_app/lib/core/settings_actions.dart:216-228). Each is pushed with course_id rewritten through the step-2 map. A negative course_id without a mapping becomes null, and the push logs "Planner event course dropped: .Sync.Events/push — '' referred to local category , which was not copied into the folder; the event is uncategorized." Each carries client_local_id = "<app>:<local id>". The folder backend upserts on it: it inserts when the key is new, and when the key exists it returns the existing folder record unchanged. A repeat push (a reconnect, or the planner and then the portal) therefore never duplicates a record and never overwrites edits made in the folder. The cloud backend has no such key (PlannerEventListCreateApiView.post creates unconditionally, backend/notes/api.py:2161-2175), so this applies to the folder backend only. After the folder confirms a record, the browser-local copy leaves the visible local list and moves to a per-app recovery list notechondria.<app>.pushed_to_folder ({folder_id, pushed_at, events, feeds}), pruned after 30 days like the local recycle bin (frontend/editor_app/lib/core/local_store.dart:136-139). It has to leave the visible list, because the portal renders local events next to backend events (frontend/portal_app/lib/core/build_page.dart:97) and would show each pushed event twice. Disconnect offers "Restore planner items pushed on ", which moves them back. Without this step a signed-in load replaces _plannerEvents and _persistLocalCache overwrites the local ones (docs/TODO.md:406-410). Whether the same push should also run for cloud sign-in (closing those TODO items) is a separate decision. The app calls applyAuthPayload({'token': 'local-folder', 'user': {..., 'is_local_folder': true}}). That flow reads /settings/, runs loadInitialData, and then pushes local courses (none are left after step 2) and drafts (app_shell_session_mixin.dart:326-327). The draft pushes upsert by client_draft_id (3.7), so a repeat is harmless, and they promote queued local:// attachments into the folder (frontend/editor_app/lib/core/note_crud.dart:192-275); a failed promotion keeps its local:// link (3.6). After a successful push each app moves the draft into its browser-local recycle bin for 30 days (frontend/editor_app/lib/core/local_trash.dart:3-12, TTL at core/local_store.dart:139). The status card says: "Browser data moved: Shared.LocalFolder/connect — drafts and planner items from this browser are now in ''; this browser keeps recoverable copies for 30 days (local recycle bin, and Disconnect → Restore)." Portal's "clear drafts" choice runs only after a fresh OAuth sign-in (frontend/portal_app/lib/core/bootstrap.dart:89-91), so connecting a folder never clears drafts.

366.body: The three stores are independent: cloud (server), browser-local (localStorage and the notechondria_attachments IndexedDB), and folder (disk). Switching changes which store the app reads. No switch deletes another store's data without keeping a recoverable copy. Connecting makes two moves, both recoverable in this browser for 30 days: browser-local drafts go to the local recycle bin, and pushed planner items go to the recovery list (7.1 steps 3 and 5). "Disconnect" forgets the handle and the remembered record, leaves the folder untouched, and never ends a cloud session (2.10 rule 4). Data otherwise moves only by explicit, idempotent pushes. The connect-time moves are owner question Q18. From, to How Status browser-local, folder Connect (7.1) v1 folder, browser-local Disconnect; optionally restore the pushed planner items (7.1) and import the folder's .nchron v1 cloud, folder Sign out of the cloud in that app (2.10 rule 2), connect the folder. Copying cloud data in: push GitHub data-sync, clone, open the clone (Phase 4 "adopt") v1 manual; in-app copy is a follow-up folder, cloud Interim: export .nchron, import it in browser-local mode, sign in; the post-login push uploads notes and courses (not history, sessions, events, or feeds). Or run backend/scripts/github_sync_restore.py on the folder (layout-compatible; needs an ntc_ key; assets are not restored, :21-24) Full-fidelity "move to cloud" is a follow-up (Q12)

368.body: Single file. createWritable(), then write(), then close(). The browser writes to a temporary file and the target changes only when close() succeeds; abort() discards (MDN createWritable). A crash mid-write leaves the old file. mode: 'exclusive' is passed when available (Chrome 121+) as a second guard behind the folder lock. package:web 1.1.1 has no mode member on FileSystemCreateWritableOptions (only keepExistingData), so the option is set through the hand-written binding (9.2). Swap files. Chrome places the temporary file next to the target, named <name>.crswap (U17). It disappears on close() or abort(); a tab that crashes mid-write can leave one behind. The scanner (3.8), the index, the folder counts in the status card (F48), the .nchron export, and the GitHub push ignore every *.crswap entry. The app never deletes one, because Chrome owns it. Why not temp file plus rename. FileSystemHandle.move() exists only on file handles in Chrome and its overwrite behavior is unverified (U5). createWritable already gives replace-on-close, so a separate rename adds nothing. MDN lists an AbortError from implementation-defined malware and safe-browsing checks among the createWritable exceptions. Attachment uploads surface it as "Attachment not saved: Shared.LocalFolder.Backend/attachments — the browser rejected the file on save (AbortError from a safe-browsing check)."

369.body: Multi-file operations use a write-ahead journal. They are: create a note (.md, .meta.json, manifest counter), delete, restore, and empty trash (3.5), delete a course, identity reassignment (3.7), and any write to a shared JSON file together with another file. Each one runs inside a single exclusive hold of the folder lock (6.2 R1): Re-read from disk every file the operation rewrites, manifest.json included (6.2 R2). The in-memory index is never the base of a write. Write .notechondria/journal/<op-id>.json: {"schema_version": 1, "op_id", "app", "created_at", "writes": [{"path", "text", "expect"}], "removals": [{"path", "expect", "directory"}]}, where "directory": true marks a recursive directory removal and is omitted for files. writes carries the full new text of every text file the operation changes, note bodies included. expect is present only for note bodies (notes/*.md, trash/notes/*.md): the size and lastModified the operation read in step 1, used by roll-forward to detect a later external edit. Attachment bytes are never journaled: they are written to their final path before the journal record, so nothing references bytes that do not exist yet. <op-id> is <UTC milliseconds, 13 digits>-<4-digit per-tab sequence>-<8 random hex>, so lexical order is creation order. Apply writes in a fixed order: note bodies, then sidecars, then the shared index files (recycle_bin.json, planner/*.json, attachments.json, history/<hex>/index.json), then manifest.json. Check that every write target exists with the journaled length. Only then apply removals, files first and directories (removeEntry(name, {recursive: true})) last. Removals always come last, so an interrupted move leaves the source in place and never loses the note. Delete the journal record. The lock is released only after this step. Roll-forward. A leftover record is replayed from step 3. Rewriting identical text is a no-op, and removing a path that is already gone (NotFoundError) is ignored, so a replay is idempotent and can itself be interrupted and replayed. Rules: Roll-forward needs the exclusive lock. Once the lock is held it re-lists .notechondria/journal/ and skips any record that no longer exists. A record that another tab is still applying never reaches roll-forward, because that tab holds the lock until step 5. A record is left over only when its tab closed or crashed mid-operation, which releases the lock (U18; a tab that stays alive holds the lock, so other tabs wait at most 5 s and fail cleanly, 6.2 R5). Leftover records are replayed one at a time in op-id order, each to completion before the next. A replay skips a write whose target already holds the journaled text. Two files may have been changed by the replay itself, so they are merged instead of overwritten: manifest.json keeps every counter at least at its value on disk, and history/<hex>/index.json keeps the entries this record's replay saved (same op_id), then prunes its pools again. External edits during replay. A record left by a crash can be replayed long after the crash, and the user may have edited a note in another editor in between. Before the replay rewrites or removes a note body that carries expect, it stats the file: size and lastModified equal expect, or the text equals the journaled text: the replay proceeds; anything else: the file was edited after the crash. The replay first saves its current text as an external_edit snapshot (3.8), in the same exclusive hold, with the record's op_id in the history index entry, and then proceeds. A second replay of the same record finds that entry and does not snapshot again. The snapshot's version id is issued above both the counter on disk and the counters the record itself journals (its manifest.json write and the ids in its history/<hex>/index.json writes). The record's manifest is written last, so a record that issued a version itself, such as a concurrent_edit snapshot journaled with a PATCH or a before_restore restore, would otherwise share that id with the replay's snapshot, and its own history body would overwrite the external text. expect lives in the record rather than in the sidecar, because a crash after step 3's sidecar writes leaves the new sidecar on disk. The same check covers removals, so a delete or trash move interrupted by a crash never discards an edit made later. It runs in the startup step (2.9), when a GET handler or a scan page finds a non-empty journal directory (6.2 R3), and before any write. Records that cannot be replayed. A record that is not a JSON object, names another op_id than its file name, or has a wrong-typed field is deleted and logged as "Folder change discarded: Shared.LocalFolder/journal — record could not be read (), so it was deleted without being replayed; the files it names keep their current contents." A record lands in one replace-on-close write before step 3, so a record this code wrote is complete or absent; one damaged later (for example a sync tool's conflict copy) is discarded the same way. A record whose schema_version is newer than this build's is not deleted and not replayed with only the fields this build knows: it stays in place and roll-forward fails with the cause "record schema_version is above , the newest this build reads; update the app to finish it", which takes the path of the next rule. If roll-forward fails (for example NotAllowedError after a revocation), readers skip every path the pending record names, and the status card shows "Folder change not finished: Shared.LocalFolder/journal — from is incomplete (); the notes it touches are hidden until Reconnect or Rescan finishes it." The scan's exclusive steps take the same path: the counter raise and every identity fix (3.7) that reads or writes a pending path are skipped, so the folder still opens and Rescan still finishes. Operations that could hold the lock for long are split into separately journaled chunks (6.2 R4). Tests (8.1, folder_journal_test.dart, over MemoryFolderFs): for each multi-file operation, inject a crash after step 2, after every single write of step 3, after step 4, and in the middle of a replay. A fresh transport over the same MemoryFolderFs must then show either the old state (crash before the record was complete) or the complete new state, never a mix. Two transports that both find one leftover record roll it forward once: the second re-checks after taking the lock and skips it. Three leftover records apply in op-id order. A crash after step 2 of a note PATCH, followed by an external edit of the .md (the fake's external-edit injection), replays to the journaled text with the external text kept as one external_edit snapshot; a second replay adds none. The same holds for a delete interrupted before its removals, and for a PATCH whose record also journals a concurrent_edit snapshot: both versions survive with distinct ids. A newer build's record stays in place and fails roll-forward; a scan with a record that keeps failing still finishes.

370.body: Operation Backend behavior Folder behavior Delete note Makes the note's live comments private (backend/notes/api.py:1598-1599), sets deleted_at, forces is_public = False, upserts a RecycleBinEntry (:1600-1603) One journaled operation: write trash/notes/<stem>.md and its sidecar with deleted_at and is_public: false; set is_public: false in every live comment note whose sidecar source_note_uuid names this note; add the pointer to recycle_bin.json; then remove notes/<stem>.md and its sidecar Restore note Clears deleted_at and removes the entry; is_public stays false (backend/notes/api.py:1941-1944) Move back to notes/ (journaled, removal last), drop the pointer, keep is_public: false. Comment notes stay private, as in the backend Empty trash Hard-deletes every trashed note and entry, no age filter (backend/notes/api.py:1948-1965). The delete cascades to NoteVersion, NoteActivitySession, and NoteAttachment (backend/notes/models.py:178-182, 213-216, 335-339) and sets source_note to null on comment notes (models.py:86-91, SET_NULL) Per trashed note, one journaled operation: remove the trashed .md and sidecar, history/<hex>/, assets/notes/<hex>/ (attachment files, attachments.json, cover), and the note's records in planner/sessions.json; set source_note_uuid: null in the sidecars of its comment notes; drop its pointer from recycle_bin.json. A large trash is chunked (6.2 R4). planner/heatmap.json holds per-day counts with no note reference, so it is unchanged Retention None; no purge constant exists in the backend None. (The 30-day TTL in frontend/editor_app/lib/core/local_store.dart:139 belongs to the separate browser-local recycle bin and is unchanged) Create with an existing client_draft_id Upserts and undeletes (backend/notes/api.py:1399-1420) Same; this makes migration pushes idempotent Delete course Hard delete. Notes, planner events, and calendar feeds of the course fall to course_id = null through SET_NULL (Note.course_id, backend/notes/models.py:28-31; PlannerEvent.course_id and CalendarFeed.course_id, backend/planner/models.py:16-19, :111-114; delete at backend/notes/api.py:933-940). Trashed notes are included, since a trashed note is a row with deleted_at set (models.py:76) In journaled chunks of at most 50 file writes: set course_slug: null in every note that names the course under notes/ and trash/notes/, and course_id: null in every record of planner/events.json and planner/feeds.json that names it; the last chunk removes courses/<slug>.json (6.2 R4). planner/sessions.json records reference notes, and the sessions handler derives course_id from the note when it answers, as note_session_payload does (backend/notes/services.py:367-374), so sessions need no change. planner/heatmap.json has no course reference After empty trash, nothing of a permanently deleted note stays in the folder: no body, no snapshot, no attachment, and no session. Copies may remain outside the folder's control, and the confirmation says so: "Permanent delete: Shared.LocalFolder.Backend/notes — notes with their history and attachments will be removed from ''. Copies in your OS trash, a sync service's file history, or earlier .nchron exports are not affected." Known difference: the backend's heatmap rows reference their note (HeatmapActivity.note_id, CASCADE, backend/planner/models.py:81-84), and build_heatmap_payload counts those rows (backend/notes/services.py:112-125). So emptying the trash lowers the backend's past heatmap counts, while the folder's per-day counts in planner/heatmap.json stay as they were.

371.body: Upload routes store bytes under assets/notes/<hex>/ and return the same JSON shape as the backend, with url set to nc-folder:///assets/notes/<hex>/attachments/<name>. The URL must differ from local://. The editor's promotion flow replaces local:// URLs with the returned url and then deletes the local:// blob (frontend/editor_app/lib/core/note_crud.dart:240-275). Returning a local:// URL would delete the file just written. A shared folderAwareImageProvider(url) returns an image provider that reads the bytes through the controller for nc-folder: and a network image otherwise. It replaces Image.network where backend media URLs are rendered: editor core/helpers.dart:309, modules/settings_build.dart:287, components/avatar.dart:41; planner core/helpers.dart:287, components/avatar.dart:31; portal core/helpers.dart:331, modules/settings_build.dart:493, components/avatar.dart:43; shared components/note_cover_image.dart:53. The existing local:// builders stay (frontend/editor_app/lib/core/helpers.dart:306-312). Planner and portal note viewers. Both build MarkdownBody without sizedImageBuilder (frontend/planner_app/lib/components/note_viewer.dart:116-121, frontend/portal_app/lib/components/note_viewer.dart:122-137). flutter_markdown 0.7.7+1's default web builder handles only http(s), data, and resource URIs; for any other scheme it calls Image.network(p.join(p.current, uri)) (lib/src/_functions_web.dart:21-77 in the 0.7.7+1 archive), so an nc-folder: image would show the error widget. Both viewers pass sizedImageBuilder: _localAttachmentImageBuilder, the builder their note editors already use (planner modules/learner_note_editor.dart:531, portal :534). That builder reaches folderAwareImageProvider through the replaced lines in planner core/helpers.dart:287 and portal core/helpers.dart:331. One line per viewer; smoke check in 8.5. Not changed: the portal startup image (frontend/portal_app/lib/components/custom_splash_overlay.dart:71). It is a device preference stored as local://app-splash/startup-image or a remote URL (frontend/portal_app/lib/modules/settings_pages.dart:453-498), never an nc-folder: URL, and it renders before any folder is open (F63). Object URLs (blob:) were considered instead; whether Flutter web's Image.network loads them is unverified (U1), so the scheme approach is the default. LocalAttachmentStore (IndexedDB notechondria_attachments, frontend/notechondria_shared/lib/src/utils/local_attachment_store_web.dart:8-10) keeps serving browser-local drafts. In folder mode new uploads go to the folder, and queued local:// attachments are promoted into the folder by the existing promotion flow (section 7.1). Promotion failure in folder mode. The promotion flow drops a draft's attachment queue whether or not each upload succeeded (frontend/editor_app/lib/core/note_crud.dart:266-268) and frees only the blobs it promoted (:270). So a failed promotion leaves a local:// link in the folder note and the bytes in this browser's LocalAttachmentStore. The link keeps rendering in this browser through the existing builder, but not in another browser or in a file manager. The folder backend logs "Attachment not copied into the folder: Shared.LocalFolder.Backend/attachments — '' stayed in this browser's storage (); the note keeps its local:// link." The status card counts folder notes whose body still contains local:// and offers "Copy browser attachments into the folder". That action uploads each blob it finds in LocalAttachmentStore and rewrites the link; a link whose blob is gone stays as is and is listed by file name. Size cap: the browser-local store caps attachments at 50 MiB (frontend/notechondria_shared/lib/src/utils/local_attachment_store.dart:219). The folder backend applies the backend's limits once they are recorded in the fixtures (section 8.4).

372.body: The apps treat negative IDs as browser-local records (frontend/editor_app/lib/core/note_loading.dart:36-42, frontend/editor_app/lib/core/note_crud.dart:90). The folder backend therefore issues positive integers per kind from manifest.json.id_counters. Each counter holds the last ID issued (0 before the first). Allocation re-reads manifest.json from disk inside the exclusive hold of the operation that writes the new record (6.2 R2), never from a cached copy. Counters never fall behind the folder. Every full scan and every adopt raises each counter to the largest ID of its kind seen in sidecars, course files, history indexes, and planner/*.json, if the counter is lower (one journaled write). Note UUIDs are version-4 UUIDs from Random.secure(). The server never adopts a client UUID: Note.uuid is UUIDField(default=uuid.uuid4, unique=True, editable=False) (backend/notes/models.py:35). A later move to the cloud creates new server IDs and UUIDs, so local values cannot collide with server ones. Duplicate identities. Copying a note in a file manager produces a second .md with the same frontmatter uuid, sometimes with a copied sidecar that repeats the id. The scanner keeps the identity on one file, chosen in this order: the file whose own sidecar (<stem>.meta.json) carries that UUID; the file whose <stem> is the UUID hex; the lexicographically first path. Every other claimant gets a new UUID, a new note ID, a new sidecar, and a rewritten frontmatter uuid, in one journaled operation. The scanner logs "Note identity reassigned: Shared.LocalFolder/scan — 'notes/' claimed uuid , which 'notes/' already uses; it now has uuid ." The same rule applies to two course files with one id or one client_course_id, and to duplicate ids inside a planner/*.json file. Adopting a GitHub data-sync clone (Phase 4). Its sidecars and course files carry the server's ids (backend/creators/services/github_sync.py:167, :226). They are unique per kind because they come from one account, so adopt keeps them and raises every counter above the largest one seen. A collision with a record already in the folder is resolved by the duplicate rule above. client_draft_id and client_course_id are kept. Folder identity. folder_id names the lock (notechondria.local_folder.<folder_id>) and the remembered-handle record, so two folders must not share it. A .nchron restore always writes a new folder_id (3.3). A folder copied in a file manager keeps the original manifest.json. When a picked folder's folder_id matches a remembered handle, the app compares the two with FileSystemHandle.isSameEntry() (bound in package:web 1.1.1; Baseline since March 2023, MDN). It needs no permission: the File System standard compares the handles' locators (section 2.2.1). Same entry: it continues. Different entry: the app has to learn whether the remembered folder still exists, and reading it needs a grant on that second handle: queryPermission({mode: 'read'}) on the remembered handle is granted (common while another tab of the origin holds the grant, or after "Allow on every visit"): the app reads its manifest.json. Readable with the same folder_id: the picked folder is a copy, and the app asks "Folder looks like a copy: Shared.LocalFolder/pick — '' has the same folder_id as ''. Give it its own identity?" Yes writes a new folder_id (journaled). NotFoundError: the folder was moved or renamed, it continues without migration (6.3), and the remembered record now holds the picked handle. Otherwise the app does not call requestPermission from the picker's click, because each browser call that needs activation is the first call of its own click handler (1.3). It asks instead: "Folder may be a copy: Shared.LocalFolder/pick — '' has the same folder_id as '', which this browser remembers, and checking '' needs access to it." The buttons are "Check ''", whose onPressed calls requestPermission({mode: 'read'}) on the remembered handle first and then reads it as above; "Give it its own identity"; and "It is the same folder, moved", which continues and replaces the remembered record. In session-only mode (the default on *.github.io, 6.1) no handle is remembered, so a copy is only detected against a handle held in the same tab. Two copies open at once in different tabs would share a lock name and change channel. That only serializes their writes and triggers extra refreshes; it cannot corrupt either folder, because every write re-reads its own folder (6.2 R2). Cross-system identity uses client_draft_id = fld_<uuid-hex> (36 characters) and client_course_id = fld_<course-uuid-hex>. Both fit the backend's max_length=64 (backend/notes/api.py:550,566), and the backend upserts on them (:766-771, :1399-1420), so pushing the same folder into an account twice does not duplicate records. Planner events and feeds pushed from browser-local storage carry client_local_id (7.1), a folder-only key. A migration to the cloud writes .notechondria/cloud_map.json (local UUID to server UUID) so deep links can be rewritten.

372.title: 3.7 IDs

373.body: On connect, the controller lists notes/, courses/, planner/, trash/, and assets/, and reads only files whose size or lastModified differ from .notechondria/index.json. The listing runs in pages under the shared lock (6.2 R4) and skips *.crswap (3.4). Scan cost for large folders is unverified (U6); the scan reports progress at least every 2 seconds. Startup uses the stored index and verifies it after the startup pass (2.9). Handlers locate notes through the in-memory index and answer the list routes from it (12.5). Each note body and sidecar entry carries the fields of the backend's note summary (index schema_version 2), so GET /notes/, course recent_notes, course notes, and the trash list read no note file; a search reads only the bodies whose title and description do not match. A single-note request re-reads only that note, plus every file it rewrites (6.2 R2). The index lacks notes that another tab or an outside program added since this tab's last scan, so the list routes, and any lookup that misses, first list notes/ (and trash/notes/) and read only the files the index lacks. This tab's own writes update the in-memory index, and the controller writes it to index.json one second after the first write of a burst, under the exclusive lock (flushIndex, 12.5), so a reload starts from them and permanently deleted notes leave the file. A scan also writes it, after applying the changes this tab made while the scan ran. Startup goes active on the stored index (2.9), but no list answers from a stored note entry before comparing it with the disk: the first listing that meets an entry loaded from index.json stats the file and reads it again only when its size or lastModified changed. A re-read note whose sidecar id, UUID, or summary fields differ from its entry gets a fresh sidecar entry. Cascades pick their targets by fields that never change (UUID, source_note_uuid, client_draft_id) and check the rest on disk; course delete first stats every note body, because course_slug can change in any tab (12.5). What stays delayed: an edit another tab or an outside program saves to an existing note after this tab compared it reaches this tab's lists at its next rescan (from Phase 4, its change message), or when this tab reads that note. A single-note request always serves what is on disk. A journal record cannot carry the body's new lastModified, so after a journaled body write the writer stamps the sidecar's md_size and md_last_modified from a fresh stat, in the same exclusive hold (stampNoteSidecar). Before overwriting a note, the backend compares the file's current lastModified and size with the sidecar's md_last_modified and md_size. If they differ, the external version is first saved as a history snapshot with reason external_edit, and the existing NoteConflictDiffView (frontend/notechondria_shared/lib/src/components/note_conflict_diff.dart:5-11) can show the difference. Concurrent edits from two tabs: the transport remembers, per note, the lastModified of the body it last served to its own tab. A PATCH that finds a different lastModified on disk first saves the disk version as a snapshot with reason concurrent_edit, then writes. Retention bounds both kinds of snapshot without touching the ones the backend would keep. The folder backend ports prune_recent_versions, which keeps the 12 newest versions of a note (backend/notes/services.py:339-344), and runs it per pool: every reason except the two below keeps the backend rule, the 12 newest of these. The apps request manual, before_restore, and autosave reasons today (autosave_1m, autosave_10m, autosave_1h; editor modules/note_editor.dart:438-446, planner modules/learner_note_editor.dart:268; labels at services.py:356-363); the folder-only reasons external_edit and concurrent_edit form a second pool with its own 12-version cap. Pruning in one pool never removes a version from the other. Two tabs saving one note in turn can therefore push out older concurrent_edit snapshots, but never a manual or autosave snapshot; within the first pool, autosaves can push out manual snapshots exactly as they do in the backend. The backend itself snapshots only on an explicit snapshot request and before a version restore (backend/notes/api.py:1899, :1918). A note holds at most 24 versions in the folder. An overwritten external or concurrent edit stays recoverable until 12 newer folder-only snapshots of that note exist. The history list shows both pools in one list, newest first. New .md files without a sidecar are adopted (with the duplicate rule in 3.7). Files that disappear are dropped from the index and logged at INFO: "Note dropped from index: Shared.LocalFolder/scan — 'notes/' no longer exists on disk." Sidecars, course files, history indexes, and manifest.json may be edited by hand. A field of the wrong type ("description": 5, "title": 7) reads as absent, so one bad value never stops a scan; the next app write of that file drops it.

375.body: An origin is scheme, host, and port; IndexedDB and Web Storage are separated by origin (MDN same-origin policy). GitHub serves project sites at https://<owner>.github.io/<repository> (GitHub Pages docs), so all Trance-0 project sites without a custom domain share one origin. Checked 2026-10-17: the GitHub API lists Pages enabled on circtime, GeometryOfMusic, MTA-strategy-optimizer, Notechondria, NoteNextra, Trance-0.github.io, and upptime. Requests to https://trance-0.github.io/{circtime,GeometryOfMusic,MTA-strategy-optimizer}/ returned 200 (same origin as Notechondria); NoteNextra and upptime redirect to their own custom domains. The Notechondria docs subtree is also on this origin. Assessment: yes, another page on the origin can read a stored handle. It can open the same IndexedDB database, take the handle, and call queryPermission. A grant belongs to the origin (the "app" in Chrome's wording), not to a page path. If a Notechondria tab still holds it (access lasts until the last tab of the origin closes) or the user chose "Allow on every visit", the call returns granted without a prompt, and the page can read, change, or delete the folder. Not storing the handle is not a full fix: a same-origin page can open or frame a Notechondria app and reach its window and prototypes while it runs. Nothing inside the origin can separate same-origin scripts. Mitigations: On *.github.io the handle is kept for the session only by default. "Remember this folder on this browser" is an unchecked opt-in (Q3). Before the first connect on that origin, a one-time notice, shown as its own dialog whose "Choose folder" button opens the picker (1.3): "Folder access is shared with this web address: Shared.LocalFolder/pick — https://trance-0.github.io also hosts other projects, and any page there could use a folder you grant. Pick a dedicated, empty folder, or use the local preview or desktop build." The picker flow recommends an empty folder and refuses a non-empty folder without manifest.json unless the user confirms a count of its entries, so the grant does not cover something like Documents. Recommend an origin without other projects: the loopback preview at http://127.0.0.1:9068 (a secure context, MDN; docs/deployment/local_preview.md, which needs a host with at least 16 GB RAM), a custom domain for the Notechondria Pages site (Q4), or an installed app, whose grant Chrome persists automatically (installability of the three apps is unverified , U7). The preview and the Docker self-host still serve uploaded media on the app origin; see the residual risk below. No cross-tab handle handoff in v1, on any origin (6.2). No tab ever sends a folder handle to another tab or answers a request for one. Residual risk on the Pages origin: while a folder is granted, a compromised or malicious page on any same-origin Trance-0 Pages project can read, modify, or delete that folder. It can do so by opening the remembered handle in IndexedDB when "Remember this folder" is on, or by opening or framing a running Notechondria app and reaching its objects. v1 has no BroadcastChannel handle handoff (6.2), so such a page cannot simply post a request and receive a live, granted handle: the answering tab could not tell a Notechondria tab from any other same-origin script. The cost is that in session-only mode each app asks for the folder once per page load (2.9; the picker's id option reopens it at the last location). The same pages can already read the cloud session token the editor and portal keep in localStorage (frontend/editor_app/lib/core/local_store.dart:275-285). Residual risk on the loopback preview and the Docker self-host: these origins host no other project, but they serve backend uploads on the app origin. The preview "forwards /api/, /media/, and /static/ to a remote Notechondria backend" on 127.0.0.1:9068 (scripts/local_remote_deploy.sh:2-4), and the self-host gateway proxies /media/ next to /editor/, /planner/, and /portal/ (deployment/docker/nginx/default.conf:5-43). Backend /media/ serves local files through django.views.static.serve or proxies R2 with the stored Content-Type (backend/notechondria/api_views.py:508-532; backend nginx uses alias with mime.types, backend/nginx/nginx.conf:55-57), and attachments accept any type up to 20 MB (backend/notes/api.py:2456, :2492). An uploaded .html or .svg, opened from a shared note's link, therefore runs as a same-origin page there, with the same reach as another Pages project has on *.github.io: the remembered handle in IndexedDB, and any app window it opens or frames. Only an origin that serves no user uploads as active content removes this risk (Q19).
