376.body: One folder serves all three apps (Q5). Which apps use it, and how that interacts with per-app cloud sessions, is in 2.10. A remembered handle lives in IndexedDB database notechondria_local_folder, keyed by folder_id. No handle handoff in v1. Each app tab obtains the handle by itself. With "Remember this folder" on, it restores the handle from IndexedDB, and because a grant belongs to the origin, queryPermission usually returns granted without a prompt while another tab of the origin holds it (6.1). In session-only mode each app tab chooses the folder once per page load (2.9). An earlier revision answered a BroadcastChannel('notechondria.local_folder') handle request on dedicated origins, on the claim that such an origin serves only Notechondria apps. That is false for both examples it named: the loopback preview and the Docker self-host serve uploaded /media/ files on the app origin (6.1). The answering tab cannot tell a Notechondria tab from such a page, and posting a handle relies on handles being structured-cloneable over BroadcastChannel, which was never verified (U13). A future handoff would need a visible confirmation in the answering tab ("Share folder '' with the planner tab?") on every origin. Lock rules. The lock is navigator.locks.request('notechondria.local_folder.<folder_id>', ...). Locks are origin-scoped and queue across tabs (MDN Web Locks). They are not re-entrant, so the transport takes the lock once at the request boundary, and handlers inside a hold call FolderFs directly. A hold lasts exactly as long as the promise the grant callback returns, so that callback returns the operation's promise and is bound with the non-guarded zone wrapper (2.5); a callback that returned nothing would release the lock before the operation's first await. R1 Modes. Exclusive: every non-GET request, journal roll-forward, .notechondria/index.json writes, counter raises, and identity reassignment (3.7). Shared (mode: 'shared'): GET handlers and each listing page of a scan. Readers therefore never see a half-applied operation. A writer waits for the current readers, and readers wait for the current writer. R2 Read-modify-write from disk. Every mutating handler re-reads from disk, inside its exclusive hold, each file it rewrites: the note's .md and sidecar, manifest.json (ID counters), recycle_bin.json, planner/events.json, planner/sessions.json, planner/feeds.json, planner/heatmap.json, the note's attachments.json, and history/<hex>/index.json. The in-memory index is a read cache for GET handlers and never the base of a write. Handlers also locate through it the notes they read or rewrite, and then re-read those files (3.8). A write that rewrites several notes selects them by a field that never changes, or after a stat of every candidate, and checks the rest on disk, so a stale entry cannot hide a target (12.5). A late or lost change message can therefore delay another tab's refresh, but it cannot lose an update. R3 Journals before reads. A GET handler or scan page that finds a non-empty .notechondria/journal/ releases its shared hold, takes the exclusive lock, re-lists the journal, rolls forward what is still there (3.4.1), takes the shared lock again, and then serves. If roll-forward fails, the reader skips every path the pending record names. A write step of the scan (counter raise, identity fix) that finds roll-forward failing skips itself when it touches one of those paths. A request that writes one of them answers 503 with "Change not saved: Shared.LocalFolder/journal — an earlier change to these files is not finished; Reconnect or Rescan finishes it first." Write handlers look notes and courses up without the skip set, so a PATCH, DELETE, or draft upsert of a pending note gets that answer, never a 404 or a second note (12.5). R4 Bounded holds. One hold targets at most 2 s (kFolderLockHoldTarget) and 50 file writes. An operation that can exceed that runs as a sequence of separately locked and journaled chunks, and every state between chunks is valid: Delete course: journaled chunks of at most 50 file writes. Each note that names the course, under notes/ and trash/notes/, gets course_slug: null; planner/events.json and planner/feeds.json each get course_id: null on every record that names the course, one file per chunk (3.5). The last chunk removes courses/<slug>.json. If interrupted, the course still exists and repeating the delete continues the work. Empty trash: one chunk per trashed note (its history and assets are removed with it), batched while the hold stays under 2 s. Archive import and adopt: chunks of 50 files. .notechondria/import.json records the archive name and progress at the start, and manifest.json is written in the last chunk. An interrupted import is a folder with import.json and no manifest, and connecting to it offers "Restart import from ''"; the writes are idempotent overwrites. Scans: listing pages of up to 500 entries per shared hold. Writers may run between pages. After the last page the scanner re-checks, under one more shared hold, every UUID it saw at two paths and every path named by a change message received during the scan, and drops stale entries. A scan during a trash move therefore never reports the note in both notes/ and trash/notes/. While a chunked operation runs, the status card shows "Folder busy: Shared.LocalFolder/ — ( of )." Other tabs' requests run between chunks. R5 Bounded waits. A request waits at most 5 s for the lock (kFolderLockWait, an AbortSignal.timeout), below the 10 s startup budget, and never past its own deadline, which runs from request start and covers every lock wait of the request, including the two re-locks of R3 (2.9). A write that times out returns 503 with "Change not saved: Shared.LocalFolder/lock — another tab held the folder lock for more than 5 s." All three apps keep such a failed save as a browser-local draft (2.8). A read that times out returns 503 with "Folder data not loaded: Shared.LocalFolder/lock — another tab held the folder lock for more than 5 s." createWritable({mode: 'exclusive'}) is a second guard; the default siloed mode would let the last writer silently win (MDN). Change channel. After each operation or chunk, the tab posts {folder_id, op_id, op, paths} on BroadcastChannel('notechondria.local_folder.changes'). Other tabs drop those index entries and, when the change touches what they show, rerun their existing load path (for example _loadInitialData), debounced to one refresh per second. The listener is bound to the controller's zone (2.5), so its refreshes never run inside a startup budget. The same channel carries the connect, disconnect, and switch messages of 2.9 and 2.10; those apply to every tab, whatever folder it has open. Two tabs editing one note: last writer wins, as in the backend, which has no optimistic-concurrency check on note PATCH. The earlier version survives as a concurrent_edit snapshot (3.8), within the 12-version bound. Tests (8.1, concurrency_test.dart): two transports over one MemoryFolderFs, sharing one in-process lock manager that implements the shared and exclusive modes, with the change channel delayed or dropped: concurrent note creates get distinct IDs, and manifest.json ends with the higher counter; concurrent event creates both land in planner/events.json; concurrent PATCHes of one note leave one version in the file and the other as a concurrent_edit snapshot; a course delete over 120 notes interleaves with a note save from the other transport, and the save succeeds within 5 s; a scan during a trash move never reports the note twice; both transports finding one leftover journal roll it forward once (3.4.1).

377.body: Situation Detection Behavior and message Startup, handle restored, grant still live queryPermission({mode: 'readwrite'}) is granted Load the index and continue (2.9) Startup, handle restored, grant expired or auto-revoked queryPermission is prompt needsPermission; the startup pass completes with the folder pending (2.9 step 4a). The reconnect view shows "Reconnect ''", whose onPressed calls requestPermission first (Chrome 122+ may offer "Allow on every visit"), and "Use browser-local mode instead", which disconnects (2.10). After more than three denials or dismissals Chrome stops showing the three-way prompt and shows the regular one (Chrome persistent-permissions post) Startup, no handle: session-only mode after a reload or in a newly opened tab, or a missing IndexedDB record Nothing to query needsPick (2.9 step 4b). The view shows "Choose '' again", whose onPressed calls showDirectoryPicker({id: 'notechondria-folder', mode: 'readwrite'}) first and only then checks the picked folder's folder_id; a different folder_id or a folder without manifest.json is refused, with "Switch to this folder" for the former (2.9). Also "Use browser-local mode instead" Startup, denied queryPermission is denied error: "Folder not opened: Shared.LocalFolder/permission — the browser denies access to ''. Choose the folder again or switch to browser-local mode." The view offers "Choose '' again" (the no-handle flow) and "Use browser-local mode instead" Revoked mid-session Any call throws NotAllowedError, or the focus check's queryPermission returns prompt This is a routine path. Besides "Remove access" in the address bar, Chrome revokes access by itself when a tab has been in the background for a while (1.4). The controller enters needsPermission; the transport answers 503 with the needsPermission message (2.8), and nothing reaches the network. A banner offers Reconnect. All three apps keep the failed save as a browser-local draft (editor core/note_crud.dart:136-160, planner core/note_crud.dart:139-158, portal core/note_crud.dart:135-150), and Reconnect pushes it (2.9). A grant made with "Allow on every visit" persists until the user revokes it Folder moved, renamed, or deleted NotFoundError on the root "Folder not found: Shared.LocalFolder/restore_handle — '' was moved, renamed, or deleted (NotFoundError). Choose the folder again or switch to browser-local mode." The view offers "Choose '' again"; a re-picked folder whose folder_id matches continues without migration, after the copy check in 3.7 These use 503, never 401 or 403, for the reason in 2.5. Mid-session the handle is still in page memory, so Reconnect works there in session-only mode too; only a new page load loses it.

378.body: Rescan on connect (for startup, the verification after the pass, 2.9), on window focus and visibilitychange (debounced to one rescan per 5 s per tab), through a recursive FileSystemObserver where it exists (desktop Chrome 133+, bound by hand because package:web 1.1.1 lacks it, 9.2; unknown and errored records force a full rescan, per the Chrome article), from a "Rescan folder" button, and before every note overwrite (3.8). A rescan is a sequence of shared-lock listing pages (6.2 R4), and it rolls forward leftover journals under the exclusive lock first (R3). On a focus rescan the controller also calls queryPermission, so a grant that Chrome revoked in the background moves the controller to needsPermission before a request fails.

384.body: Unit tests in frontend/notechondria_shared/test/local_folder/: codecs, router, journal crash and roll-forward tests including the replay external-edit check (3.4.1), two-transport concurrency tests (6.2), ID allocation and duplicate identities (3.7), trash semantics and the empty-trash cascade (3.5), course delete over notes, trashed notes, events, and feeds (3.5), snapshot pools (3.8), scans of hand-edited files with wrong-typed fields (3.8), recurrence and search ports, archive bridge, the secret denylist in both directions (5), the per-device settings filter (F08), the detail-sentinel check (2.5), decideStorageMode over seeded SharedPreferences (2.8), the opening hold and the deadlines (2.9), and the StorageModeClient routing table (2.8). T6 (design review 3) is resolved by a CI step: .github/workflows/frontend-pages.yml runs flutter test test/local_folder/ -r compact from frontend/notechondria_shared ("Test notechondria_shared local folder", after the three app builds, in the job that already installs Flutter), so the journal, concurrency, identity, denylist, and storage-mode tests gate every Pages deploy. The step relies on flutter test resolving packages: an explicit flutter pub get in that package exits 1 on its l10n generation with Flutter 3.44 ("Placeholders used in selects must be of type 'String'"). The rest of the shared package's tests stay out of CI. Per-app smoke tests (CI), 8.5. OPFS and Web Locks integration tests in Chromium (8.3), run in a Docker container with the Flutter SDK and Playwright's Chromium, on a host with at least 16 GB RAM, and not in GitHub CI unless the owner adds a job (Q13). They cover what only a browser can show: that the locks.request wrapper keeps the lock for the whole operation (2.5), and that a throwing void listener reaches the zone's error handler. Manual checks on desktop Chrome (8.6).

385.body: MemoryFolderFs implements FolderFs, with injectable failures (NotAllowedError, NotFoundError, abort mid-write, external edit with a new lastModified), revoke() and grant() to simulate a lost and restored permission, and crash points ("throw after the n-th write"). MemoryFolderLocks is the matching Web Locks double, with shared and exclusive modes and abort timeouts, shared by several transports, and a change channel double that can delay or drop messages. MemoryHandleStore holds remembered handles, and MemoryFolderPicker returns a preset MemoryFolderFs root or throws AbortError, standing in for "Choose '' again". MemoryFolderPlatform bundles these for LocalFolderController.forTest(app:, boot:, platform:), which is what smoke tests pass as NotechondriaApp(localFolder: ...) (2.7). They are exported from a separate library, package:notechondria_shared/local_folder_testing.dart, so production code never imports them. The fake sits at the FolderFs level because package:web types are extension types and cannot be mocked by implementing them (dart.dev package:web page). MemoryFolderLocks keeps a lock for as long as the Dart operation runs, so it cannot show the JavaScript return-value bug of 2.5; 8.3 covers that in Chromium.

386.body: The test file is frontend/notechondria_shared/test/local_folder_opfs_test.dart. It lands in Phase 1 with the web FolderFs and the lock wrapper, gains attachment-byte tests in Phase 2 and archive-bridge tests in Phase 4, and runs from frontend/notechondria_shared. const bool kLocalFolderOpfsTestHook = bool.fromEnvironment('NOTECHONDRIA_TEST_OPFS_FOLDER'); defaults to false. Only when it is true does the web FolderFs take its root from navigator.storage.getDirectory() (a per-test subdirectory) and report permissions as granted. Run with flutter test --platform chrome --dart-define=NOTECHONDRIA_TEST_OPFS_FOLDER=true test/local_folder_opfs_test.dart. Lock tests, over the real navigator.locks and the production folder_lock_web.dart wrapper: two overlapping exclusive requests on one name, the first awaiting several timers (about 200 ms in total) before it returns: the second starts only after the first returns, and navigator.locks.query() taken during the first lists one held and one pending request; an operation that throws: the caller receives the error, and a following request on the same name is granted at once, with nothing left in query().held; two shared holds overlap, and an exclusive request waits for both; a lock wait longer than its AbortSignal.timeout (shortened for the test) fails with the folder-lock message (6.2 R5); a throwing BroadcastChannel listener reaches the zone's error handler. Checked in Phase 1a by swapping in a guarded (void) wrapper in a scratch copy: the first, third, and fourth tests fail (the lock is released before the operation's first await), so they are the regression test for 2.5. The second passes either way, because a guarded wrapper releases the lock even earlier. Where it runs: in a Docker container with the Flutter SDK (the version CI pins) and Playwright's Chromium, with CHROME_EXECUTABLE pointing at that Chromium. docs/AGENTS.md allows Flutter containers only on hosts with at least 16 GB RAM, so the run follows its host resource budget: measure free -h and nproc first, cap the container (docker run --rm --memory=6g --cpus=2 ...), wrap the test in timeout 1200, run one container at a time, and kill it after 5 minutes without output. Fallback if it runs out of memory or hangs: run only the VM tests and the manual checks in 8.6, and say so in the round summary. GitHub CI does not run these tests unless the owner adds a Chrome job (Q13). Working recipe (Phase 1a, Flutter 3.44.0, Chromium 131): a derived image FROM mcr.microsoft.com/playwright/python:v1.49.1-noble with COPY --from=ghcr.io/cirruslabs/flutter:stable /sdks/flutter /sdks/flutter, apt-get install unzip xz-utils, flutter precache --web at build time, and CHROME_EXECUTABLE set to a two-line wrapper that runs /ms-playwright/chromium-1148/chrome-linux/chrome --no-sandbox "$@" (the container runs as root). The repo is copied to a scratch directory and mounted there, never read-write. Run, with no -p mapping: docker run --rm --memory 6g -v <scratch>:/work ... flutter test --platform chrome --dart-define=NOTECHONDRIA_TEST_OPFS_FOLDER=true test/local_folder_opfs_test.dart. The network stays on because the web test runner runs pub get for flutter_tools; with --network none it stops with "Failed to update packages". Sampling /proc/net/tcp during the run showed only 127.0.0.1 listeners (the test server and Chrome's DevTools port). On this host docker run --cpus fails (cgroup v2 in threaded mode) and --memory is accepted but not enforced ("Limitation discarded"), so the bound is the timeout wrapper and one container at a time. Result: 7 of 7 passed; the whole container run took about 25 s. Timing check (phase 1b review P1B-1, 12.5): test/local_folder_opfs_timing_test.dart seeds 2,000 notes on OPFS, opens the folder with the real Web Locks wrapper, and times each route through the transport, reading the lock holds from onHold. It fails when any timed step holds the lock for 2 s or more (kFolderLockHoldTarget, 6.2 R4): the single-note GET and PATCH by id and UUID, the first list after the open from index.json (which stats every stored entry), the note page, all notes, search, courses, the draft upsert, note delete, the index.json flush, course delete (which stats every note body), and a page with 300 notes the index lacks. The single-note routes must also answer within 2 s. Only printed, not checked: the seed time, the first open's full scan and its longest hold, and the open from index.json. It runs in the same container command, after the OPFS test file. 0.1.200's full reads answered a single-note GET with the 8 s read deadline's 503 (hold 11 s); the numbers after the change are in 12.5. Unreachable in production: the flag is a compile-time constant, and the release builds pass only APP_VERSION (.github/workflows/frontend-pages.yml:63,73,83, .github/workflows/portal-release.yml:134-156), so the compiler drops the branch. An optional CI guard greps each built main.dart.js for the hook's marker string (Q13). How OPFS handles answer queryPermission is unverified (U10); the hook does not depend on it.

387.body: One sanitized backend response per (a) and (b) route lives in frontend/notechondria_shared/test/fixtures/api_v1/, and a unit test asserts that the local router returns the same keys and JSON types for the same request. Phase 1 fixtures are hand-written. No host available to this work can run the backend: docs/AGENTS.md bans local containers below 16 GB RAM, and the host Python is 3.14 against 3.11-era pins. Each fixture is built from the serializer or payload helper that renders its route: backend/notes/api.py (NoteSummarySerializer :344, NoteDetailSerializer :423, CourseSerializer :450, NoteVersionSerializer :573, CalendarFeedSerializer :631), backend/creators/api.py (the settings representation at :395-428), and the payload helpers in backend/notes/services.py (for example note_session_payload :367). Each one is checked against the assertions in backend/notes/tests.py and backend/creators/tests.py. A _source key names the serializer and the backend test it was checked against; the comparison ignores keys that start with _. Q14's backend test is the CI recorder. backend/notes/test_api_contract.py runs in backend-tests.yml (python manage.py test). It seeds one creator's data, calls each fixture's route with the Django test client, and fails when a key or JSON type differs from the committed fixture. It also writes every live response under backend/build/contract_responses/, which an actions/upload-artifact step publishes, so a fixture can be refreshed from CI without a local backend. The fixture directory joins the workflow's paths: filter (.github/workflows/backend-tests.yml:16-19), so a fixture-only change runs the test. Format (0.1.200). Each file holds _source, _setup (empty, course_and_note, or trashed_note, seeded the same way through the API on both sides), request (method, path, optional body, with {course_id}, {note_id}, and {note_uuid} replaced by the seeded ids), status, and body. _folder_omits lists dotted key paths the folder leaves out on purpose (the per-device settings of F08, also inside app_settings), and _backend_route: false marks the two routes below. Null on either side is compatible, and list elements are compared when both lists are non-empty. The Dart side is test/local_folder/fixtures_contract_test.dart. Phase 1 has 21 fixtures; Q14's test passed against all 19 backend routes in a python:3.11-slim container before the first push (12.4). Routes the backend does not have (GET /auth/session/, POST /auth/logout/, Q17) get no recorder. Their shapes come from the client code that parses them. _restoreSession reads authenticated and passes the whole map to applyAuthPayload (editor core/auth_flows.dart:174-177, portal core/bootstrap.dart:325-328), which reads token and user (app_shell_session_mixin.dart:181-182). The session fixture is therefore {"authenticated": true, "token": "<the request's token>", "user": {<the GET /settings/ profile keys>, "is_local_folder": true}}. Logout's response is decoded and discarded (editor core/http_client.dart:695-704), so its fixture is {}.

388.body: CI runs only test/smoke_test.dart per app (.github/workflows/frontend-pages.yml:59,69,79). Each app adds test/local_folder_smoke.dart with registerLocalFolderSmokeTests(), called from smoke_test.dart's main, so the CI file grows by two lines (planner's is already 767 lines). Harness. Each folder-mode check boots NotechondriaApp(localFolder: LocalFolderController.forTest(...)) over MemoryFolderPlatform (8.2) with no client, so the production default-client line runs (2.7). The whole test body, including pumpWidget and every pump, runs inside http.runWithClient(body, () => recorder) (package:http 1.6.0 client.dart:228). recorder is a BaseClient that records every request and fails the test on any request outside the passthrough check below. The precedence check, which starts in cloud mode on purpose, uses the smoke tests' existing fake backend (MockClient(backend.handle)) as the zone client instead. Client() returns the zone's client first (client.dart:42), so the recorder is what StorageModeClient's inner client, a multipart request.send() (base_request.dart:141), and a top-level http.get (http.dart:168) all receive: a missed multipart site or a stray http.* call fails the test instead of escaping it. package:http warns that Flutter does not guarantee which zone runs a callback (client.dart:219-226), so setUp also sets HttpOverrides.global to an override whose createHttpClient fails the test (restored in tearDown); a dart:io client created outside the zone fails too. Timing checks run on the test's fake clock. Phases. The editor file lands in Phase 1 with client-level checks (HttpNotechondriaClient(httpClient: controller.httpClient) built inside the same zone) and gains the app-level checks in Phase 2; the planner and portal files land in Phase 3. The Phase 1 file (0.1.200) has three checks: note create, edit, delete, restore, and empty trash in the folder, with the handshake, ping, and a multipart upload (501 until Phase 2) answered in the page; revoked mid-session; and the passthrough. Each asserts what reached the recorder, with HttpOverrides.global failing any dart:io client. Editor: create a note and find notes/<hex>.md with frontmatter and a sidecar; edit, delete to trash/notes/, restore; upload an attachment and get an nc-folder: URL; take a snapshot; empty trash and find no history/<hex>/ or assets/notes/<hex>/ left. Planner: a weekly event yields occurrences in /activity/week/; an .ics import lands in planner/feeds/; an event created signed out, with a local course, is present after connect with the folder course ID; a second connect push leaves one copy (7.1). Portal: the front page renders from folder data; course reorder persists; a .nchron export has the v1 buckets and folder/; local events pushed at connect appear once. Planner and portal: a note whose body has ![x](nc-folder:///assets/notes/<hex>/attachments/a.png) renders in the note viewer as an Image with a memory provider and without the "failed to load" text (3.6). All, revoked mid-session (2.8): open a note, call memoryFs.revoke(), then save the note (PATCH with content), upload an attachment (multipart), run _loadInitialData, apply settings (which calls updateBaseUrl with the cloud URL), run the version probe, and run ping. Assert that the recorder holds zero requests, that each failed request carried the needsPermission detail, that the save became a browser-local draft, and that the token is still the folder token (no session clearing). Repeat with the folder state forced to needsPick, scanning, error, and disconnected. All, passthrough: inside runCloudVersionCheck, one GET /api/v1/handshake/ reaches the recorder with no Authorization header; a PATCH /api/v1/notes/1/ made inside the same zone does not. All, startup bounds (2.9): with another transport holding the lock for 7 s, startup completes, the waiting request gets the 5 s folder lock message, and no "Cloud data not loaded" text appears. A start with the permission at prompt shows the reconnect view and sends no shell request. A GET that meets a leftover journal while another transport holds the lock answers by its 8 s deadline from request start, across the R3 re-locks. Portal, cold deep links (2.8 rule 4): with a folder that holds note U and an index, the app starts at /note/<U> (through tester.binding.platformDispatcher.defaultRouteNameTestValue). _NoteRoutePage renders U's title and body, and the recorder holds zero requests. A cold start at /notes shows the folder's notes in the learner tab after the guest fetch, again with zero requests. Repeated at /note/<U> with no remembered handle, the route page shows the reconnect view; after MemoryFolderPicker returns the same folder, U renders. All, choose again (2.9): with no remembered handle, startup shows "Choose '' again" and sends no request. MemoryFolderPicker then returns, in separate runs: the same folder, and the app reaches active; a folder with another folder_id, and the refusal appears with the shared key unchanged, after which "Switch to this folder" rewrites the key and the change-channel double receives {op: "switch"}; an empty folder, and the refusal appears with the folder still empty; AbortError, and the view stays. Editor and portal, precedence (2.10): with a saved cloud session in notechondria.<app>.session and the shared key set to a folder, both seeded through SharedPreferences.setMockInitialValues before LocalFolderBoot.preload() so that decideStorageMode runs, the app starts in cloud mode (its session check reaches the fake backend), shows the "Local folder not used" notice, and keeps the session. In folder mode with another app's session key seeded, Disconnect leaves that key byte-identical and the recorder holds no request (no /auth/logout/). All, Disconnect order (2.10 rule 4): with a note edit pending, Disconnect; the edit is kept as a browser-local draft, and the recorder holds zero requests, so no request carried Token local-folder after the mode switched. All: an injected unqualified probe shows the option disabled with the noDirectoryPicker message.

389.body: Pages origin: the option is enabled; Firefox shows it disabled with the message. Connect an empty folder; the notice's "Choose folder" opens the picker; the files appear in the OS file manager. Non-empty folder without a manifest asks for confirmation; a system folder is refused by Chrome. Create, edit, delete, restore, and empty trash; check files on disk, including that history/ and assets/ of the deleted note are gone. Edit a note's .md in another editor; the app shows the change after focus, and history holds an external_edit snapshot. Editor, planner, and portal open in three tabs; save in two at once; no file is corrupted. Close all tabs and reopen. With "Remember this folder" on: "Reconnect ''" appears (and "Allow on every visit"). With it off, the default on https://trance-0.github.io: "Choose '' again" appears, the picker opens at the folder's location, and choosing the folder resumes with every note present. Remove access from the address-bar icon mid-edit, and separately leave the tab in the background until Chrome revokes access; in both cases the edit survives as a draft and syncs after Reconnect. Move or rename the folder; the not-found message appears; re-pick works. Attachments, covers, and the avatar render, also in the planner and portal note viewers. .ics import; URL subscribe to a Google calendar shows the CORS message; a CORS-enabled feed works. .nchron export, then import into a new empty folder: identical tree except a new folder_id. GitHub push with a fine-grained token; the token is in no file or log. Same flow at http://127.0.0.1:9068. With "Remember this folder" on, a second app opened in a new tab opens the folder without a prompt while the first tab is still open; with it off, each app asks once per page load, on this origin as on https://trance-0.github.io. No tab ever receives a handle from another tab. Copy a note file and, separately, the whole folder in the file manager: the copied note gets its own UUID after a rescan, and picking the copied folder offers its own identity (3.7). Session-only, wrong folder: after a reload, "Choose '' again", then pick a different Notechondria folder. The refusal names both folders and nothing changes on disk. "Switch to this folder" opens it, and an open planner tab shows the "Folder switched in another tab" banner. Picking an empty folder shows the refusal and leaves the folder empty in the file manager. Locks: open the editor and the planner on one folder. In the editor, empty a trash of 100 or more notes, and while the status card shows "Folder busy", save a note in the planner and run await navigator.locks.query() in the planner's DevTools console: held lists notechondria.local_folder.<folder_id> once, as exclusive, and the planner's request is under pending; the save completes after the chunk. Then remove folder access from the address bar during an editor save: within a second, navigator.locks.query() shows nothing held, and after Reconnect the planner's next save succeeds.

391.body: Each phase is one or more normal rounds: VERSION bump, docs/versions/<v>.md plus its docs/SUMMARY.md entry, and the docs/LLM_CHECK.md round log (docs/AGENTS.md, round-end convention). An app's wiring lands in the phase that ships its sign-in option: its local_folder startup step, prepare: LocalFolderBoot.preload in main.dart, the controller and StorageModeClient default client in _NotechondriaAppState with the NotechondriaApp(localFolder:) test seam, the settings gating (including onPing and the GitHub card gate), and its app-level smoke checks. An app without that wiring ignores the shared mode key (main 2.10 rule 1), so it never calls a folder route that does not exist yet. Within a wired app, every control whose route arrives in a later phase or is cloud-only is gated with cloudOnly(...) (cloudOnlyAction(...) for a required action callback), the shared session mixin's helpers; the GitHub card is gated until Phase 5 (9.3), and F18's template restore stays gated (T7(f)). Both gates were placed in Phase 1 and stay inert until an app's localFolder is set (12.4). The editor gets its option at the end of Phase 2, the planner and portal at the end of Phase 3. Until an app's option ships, nothing can write the key for it, so no feature flag is needed (AGENTS.md 1.2). Spike, nothing merged. Resolve U1, U3, U5, U7, U10, U17, and U18 (section 11.1) in a throwaway build on desktop Chrome. Foundation. FolderFs (web, memory, stub), JS bindings with the per-callback zone wrappers (main 2.5), qualification, handle store, the pick flow (the isSameEntry copy check, "Choose again" with its folder_id checks and "Switch to this folder"), lock (shared and exclusive modes), controller (with the opening and needsPick states), LocalFolderBoot and the runGuardedApp(prepare:) hook, journal (with expect and the replay check), layout and index (chunked scans, duplicate identities), note codec, transport (the opening hold, 503 states, read and write deadlines from request start), StorageModeClient (routing and the handshake passthrough), router, handlers for handshake, settings (with the per-device key filter), session, Casdoor config, courses (delete over notes, trashed notes, events, and feeds), notes, and trash (with the cascade); the secret denylist; the AuthHub slot, sign-in option, status card (with folder counts and bytes), reconnect view, and banners. The startup-budget condition in HttpClientInternalsMixin.send and disconnectFolder() in the session mixin. Behavior-preserving fixes for all three apps: the multipart _httpClient.send(request) sites and the optional pingBackend client. Editor smoke checks at the client level: the editor's real HttpNotechondriaClient over the controller's StorageModeClient and MemoryFolderPlatform, inside http.runWithClient, with no app wiring, so the shell cannot yet read the mode key. The Chromium lock tests in test/local_folder_opfs_test.dart (8.3). Hand-written fixtures for these routes and Q14's backend contract test (8.4). No app wiring in any app. Phase 1 decisions (design review 3 T7): (a) one session-key table keyed by app id, kAppSessionKeys in local_folder_boot.dart; (b) decideStorageMode takes isWeb from the LocalFolderPlatform that forTest receives; (c) the session mixin reaches the controller through an abstract LocalFolderController? get localFolder that each shell implements (null until its wiring phase), a one-line app edit allowed in Phase 1; (d) the external_edit/concurrent_edit snapshot writer and the two-pool prune are Phase 1 (folder_snapshots.dart); (e) .notechondria/index.json is a derived cache with schema_version 1, layout_version, folder_id, generated_at, and per-path entries (schema in folder_index.dart), and any other index is ignored and rescanned; (f) F18 template restore answers 501 in folder mode and its callback is gated with cloudOnlyAction(...), so the GitHub card is not the only gated control; (g) a granted handle without manifest.json is error with "Folder not opened: Shared.LocalFolder/scan — '' has no manifest.json () ..."; (h) a lock wait cut short by the request deadline answers with the 2.9 deadline message ("waiting for the folder lock"), and only a full 5 s wait uses R5's; (i) in disconnected, a GET gets "Folder data not loaded: Shared.LocalFolder/disconnect — '' was disconnected in this tab; the app reloads its browser-local data instead."; (j) when both 3.8 checks trip on one PATCH, one external_edit snapshot is taken. Landed in 0.1.200 (the Phase 1a storage core, then Phase 1b), with the option hidden in every app; the differences from this text are listed in 12.4. Content. Attachments, covers, avatar, folderAwareImageProvider, promotion-failure handling and "Copy browser attachments into the folder", history and snapshots (external_edit, concurrent_edit, in their own pool), sessions, search port, front page. Editor wiring (as listed above) and its app-level smoke checks. Show the option in the editor. Planner. Events and recurrence, deadlines, week view, heatmap, calendar import, URL fetch with the CORS fallback, the client_local_id upsert, and the connect-time push of browser-local courses, events, and feeds with the recovery list (main 7.1). Planner and portal wiring (as listed above), the sizedImageBuilder line in both note viewers, the portal's _NoteRoutePage controller and reconnect view, and their smoke files. Show the option in the planner and portal. Interchange and multi-tab. .nchron bridge (new folder_id on restore, chunked import), change channel, FileSystemObserver and focus rescans, "adopt a GitHub data-sync clone". No handle handoff (main 6.2). GitHub (b). Credential store and token-based status, repos, push, and course repo bind and import. The GitHub card's cloudOnly(...) gate is replaced by the token-based card in folder mode.

The copy check needs no permission for isSameEntry and asks before probing a remembered handle without a grant. disconnectFolder() moves the state to disconnected and clears the token before the mode switches 2.10, 3.7, 7.1, 8.3, 8.4, 8.5, 9.2, Q14 Resolved differently from the review's literal wording: N1 offered a pending mode or a synchronous decision. The design uses both parts: the mode is decided synchronously, and a separate folder state, opening, holds requests while the folder is opened. Holding (instead of answering 503) is what lets a cold portal deep link render the folder note. N8 offered a write deadline or dropping the claim. The design adds the deadline and also narrows the claim, because a started write cannot be cut off safely. N11 offered an exemption or coalescing. The design uses separate pools, which keeps every automatic snapshot up to its own cap and needs no timing rule. N15 suggested comparing the body with the pre-op sidecar. The record stores the expected size and lastModified instead, because a crash after step 3's sidecar writes leaves the new sidecar on disk. N2 named Zone.current; the design binds the lock callback in the zone of the request that asked for the lock, which is Zone.current at the call, and keeps the controller's captured zone for void listeners only. Also changed while verifying: Sections 11 and 12 moved out of the main document into unverified_and_sources.md and this file, because the revision would otherwise have taken the main document past 1000 lines. Nothing was deleted; the main document keeps a pointer for each. 6.3's "denied" row said the folder becomes "Disconnected", while 2.9 step 5 said error. Both now say error, with "Choose '' again" and "Use browser-local mode instead". The connect, disconnect, and switch messages of the change channel move to Phase 1, because the 2.10 rule 5 banners and the 2.9 switch notice need them before Phase 4's change messages. 9.2's totals are recomputed from the table: about 8,500 shared library lines in 46 files (the review summed revision 1's table to about 7,900 against a stated 7,500). 9.3's fallback range for the planner's case 3: settings builder is corrected to app_shell.dart:813-927; the _SettingsPage(...) call runs to :927, past githubSyncCardBuilder at :897. U18 is narrowed to the renderer-crash case: release on tab close is specified (Web Locks spec, section 2.6). 3.5 records a known difference found while checking N10: the backend's heatmap rows reference the note (HeatmapActivity.note_id, CASCADE, backend/planner/models.py:81-84), so empty trash lowers its heatmap, while the folder's per-day counts do not change. 404.body: The Phase 1b review (.agents/tasks/phase1b-review.json, P1B-1 to P1B-5) and the open item of the 1a review (P1A-7), resolved before Phase 2 shows the option. The option is still hidden, so no app changes. ID Resolution Where P1B-1 Handlers locate notes through the in-memory index and re-read only the note they serve or rewrite. Index schema_version 2 adds a summary to note body and sidecar entries (the fields of the backend's note summary), so the list routes read no note file; a search reads only the bodies its title and description miss, 32 at a time. The list routes, and any lookup that misses, first list notes/ (and trash/notes/) and index only the files the index lacks. This tab's writes update the in-memory index from the text they wrote and a fresh stat, and reach index.json through the coalesced flush of L2A-1 below. Chromium, 2,000 notes on OPFS: a single-note GET took 27 ms (21 ms hold) and a PATCH 59 ms (56 ms hold); 0.1.200 answered the same GET with the 8 s deadline's 503 after an 11 s hold. A search took 1.3 s, so it passes the 2 s hold target near 3,000 notes (Phase 2 search port, docs/development/local_folder_mode/deferred.md) 3.8, 6.2 R2 R4, 8.3; folder_index.dart, handlers/lookup.dart, handlers/{records,notes,courses,trash}.dart, transport.dart, local_folder_controller.dart P1B-2 checkCloudVersion treats an answer carrying x-notechondria-backend: local-folder as not checked: "Cloud version not checked: Shared.LocalFolder/version_check — folder mode sends the update check only to an https URL or a loopback http URL, so GET /api/v1/handshake/ was answered in this page and nothing was sent." 2.8 rule 3; storage_mode_client.dart, folder_messages.dart P1B-3 Write lookups of notes and courses ignore the skip set of a failed roll-forward (lookupSkip), so commit and writeText answer writeBlockedByJournal instead of a 404 or a second note for the same client_draft_id 6.2 R3; handlers/lookup.dart, handlers/notes.dart, handlers/courses.dart P1B-4 The transport passes every 404 and 501 detail, router or handler, through scrubRouteDetail 2.5; transport.dart P1B-5 Tests for the session mixin's folder branches (applyAuthPayload, the logout() guard, disconnectFolder(), cloudOnly, cloudOnlyAction), a throwing prepare, the write-start deadline, and the transport-level R3 path 8.1; test/local_folder/app_wiring_test.dart, transport_test.dart P1A-7 Closed in 0.1.200 by the per-character fold (12.4); the review's invalid to\u212Aen case is now in messages_test.dart. The scrub now resumes at the second character of a match instead of after the whole match, so overlapping sentinels ("invalid token_not_valid") are all broken 2.5; folder_messages.dart The review of these changes (.agents/tasks/review-2a.json, L2A-1 to L2A-7) found that the index, now the source of list rows, was trusted where it could be out of date. Its fixes: ID Resolution Where L2A-1 index.json follows this tab's writes: flushIndex writes the in-memory index under the exclusive lock one second after the first write of a burst (kIndexFlushDelay), so a reload starts from them and permanently deleted notes leave the file; a failed write logs "Folder index not saved: Shared.LocalFolder/write — ..." and is retried after the next write. Startup still goes active on the stored index (2.9), but its note body and sidecar entries start unverified: the first listing that meets one stats the file and reads it again only when its size or lastModified changed, and course payloads run that listing too. Chromium, 2,000 OPFS notes: the first list after an open from index.json held the lock 1,733 ms (later lists 92 ms), the flush 113 ms 3.8, 6.2 R1; local_folder_controller.dart, handlers/lookup.dart, handlers/courses.dart, folder_index.dart, transport.dart, router.dart L2A-2 A rescan records the index changes this tab makes while it runs and applies them to its entries in its final exclusive hold, before index.json is written, and again for changes made after that hold 3.8; local_folder_controller.dart, folder_scanner.dart, folder_index.dart L2A-3 A re-read note whose sidecar id, UUID, or summary fields differ from its entry gets a fresh sidecar entry (one stat, only on a difference), so another tab's description edit reaches the list and a renumbered id is found once the old id is asked for 3.7, 3.8; handlers/lookup.dart L2A-4 Note delete selects comments by source_note_uuid only and checks is_public on disk 3.5, 6.2 R2; handlers/notes.dart L2A-5 Course delete stats every note body (500 per hold) before it selects by course_slug, and indexes again each body that changed. Chromium, 2,000 notes: 11 holds, the longest 217 ms, 969 ms in all 3.5, 6.2 R2 R4; handlers/courses.dart, handlers/lookup.dart L2A-6 Not bounded yet: the first list after an open and a listing that finds many new files run in one hold. Measured 1,733 ms for 2,000 stored notes and 626 ms for 300 new ones, so about 2,300 stored notes or 900 new files pass the 2 s target. Read batches of 128 instead of 32 changed little (1,615 ms). Tracked in docs/development/local_folder_mode/deferred.md for Phase 4's paged rescans 6.2 R4; docs/development/local_folder_mode/deferred.md L2A-7 The Chromium timing test asserts every timed step's hold against kFolderLockHoldTarget; testing.md 8.3 names the numbers that are only printed 8.3; test/local_folder_opfs_timing_test.dart

Item Code Where Image provider folderAwareImageProvider(url, folder:) returns FolderImage (bytes read through the controller's FolderFs, decoded as MemoryImage decodes) for nc-folder: and NetworkImage otherwise; folderAwareSvg uses SvgPicture.memory or SvgPicture.network (T4). Only paths under assets/ are read; a ?v= query is dropped from the path and kept in the cache key. flutter_svg becomes a direct dependency of the shared package (the three apps already had it) 3.6, 9.2; utils/folder_aware_image.dart, pubspec.yaml Upload writes LocalHandlerContext.writeBytes writes an attachment, cover, or avatar file (replace-on-close, 3.4) before the journaled JSON that names it, so an interruption leaves at most an unreferenced file 3.4.1, 3.6; router.dart, transport.dart, handlers/attachments.dart Attachment names Stored names keep letters, digits, ., _, and - (others become _), lose a leading dot, are capped at 120 characters, and get -2, -3 on a clash; attachments.json also keeps original_filename, which the payload answers. Size caps are the backend's: 20 MB per attachment, 5 MB per cover; the avatar, which has no backend cap, uses 20 MB 3.6; handlers/attachments.dart Covers and avatar assets/notes/<hex>/cover.<ext> and assets/avatar.<ext>; the stored URL carries ?v=<ms> so a replaced file is not served from the image cache, and a replaced file with another extension is removed in the same journal record. The backend also bumps last_edit on a cover change; the folder leaves the note body alone 3.6, F09, F34 History GET /notes/{id}/history/ lists both retention pools, newest first (at most 24 entries); the backend answers its 12 newest. Each index entry also keeps the sidecar's description and metadata_json, so a restore brings them back; a folder-only snapshot has neither, and the note keeps its own 3.8, F23; handlers/history_sessions.dart, folder_snapshots.dart Sessions planner/sessions.json records carry note_uuid besides note_id, so empty trash finds them; course_id is derived from the note when answering. Every score needs the note content, so a search reads every body (Phase 1 read only those the title and description missed). Draft upserts are edits, which build_heatmap_payload does not count. The day is the device's local day F38, 3.5; handlers/activity.dart, handlers/notes.dart Front page Carousel and collections: the folder's courses that hold at least one live note (the backend: at least one public note), in course order, at most 6; recent and recommended notes: every live note by last_edit (D1); upcoming_events from planner/events.json without client_local_id. GET /heatmap/ (182 days each way) is answered too F44; handlers/activity.dart Handshake capabilities.attachments is 1 F46; handlers/auth_settings.dart Fixtures 14 new fixtures. 407.body: Phase 0 spike, U3 (Phase 2): a real click on the Flutter "Use a local folder" button keeps transient activation until showDirectoryPicker, on both the semantics and the pointer path, in headless Chromium 131 (unverified_and_sources.md 11.1). The other spike items are on the manual list under "Deferred from Phase 2". Phase 1b review follow-ups (.agents/tasks/phase1b-review.json), landed before Phase 2 shows the option (design revision_log.md 12.5): P1B-1 (MEDIUM): note and course lookups read every note inside the lock. Lookups now go through the in-memory index (schema 2 holds the note summary fields) and re-read only the note served or rewritten. Chromium timing over 2,000 OPFS notes (test/local_folder_opfs_timing_test.dart): single-note GET 27 ms, PATCH 59 ms; 0.1.200 answered the same GET with a 503 after 8 s. P1B-2: "Check for updates" no longer counts a locally answered handshake (x-notechondria-backend: local-folder) as a cloud answer. P1B-3: after a failed roll-forward, write lookups skip nothing, so a PATCH, DELETE, or draft upsert of the pending note answers writeBlockedByJournal. P1B-4: scrubRouteDetail on every 404 and 501 detail in LocalFolderTransport._detail. P1B-5: tests for the inert folder branches, a throwing prepare, the 7 s write start, and the transport R3 path. P1A-7 (LOW): closed in 0.1.200; the invalid to\u212Aen test added, and overlapping sentinels are now broken too. Loop 2a review follow-ups (.agents/tasks/review-2a.json, design revision_log.md 12.5; review-2a-pass2.json APPROVED and marks L2A-1 to L2A-5 and L2A-7 fixed, with the residues listed below): L2A-1 (MEDIUM): index.json was written only by scans and trusted on open, so a reload listed pre-edit rows. The in-memory index is now flushed to index.json 1 s after this tab's first write of a burst, and stored note entries are compared with the disk by the first listing that meets them. L2A-2: a rescan keeps the index changes this tab made while it ran. L2A-3: a re-read note whose sidecar differs from its entry gets a fresh entry (another tab's description edit, a renumbered id). L2A-4: note delete picks comments by source_note_uuid and checks is_public on disk. L2A-5: course delete stats every note body before it selects by course_slug. L2A-7: the Chromium timing test asserts every route's hold. Search hold: Phase 1's substring search read every body its title and description missed, in batches of 32, and held the shared lock 1.2 to 1.3 s over 2,000 OPFS notes in headless Chromium. The Phase 2 note_search_score port reads every body (each score needs the content) and was not timed in Chromium. Bound it (body cache, or chunked holds within the 8 s read deadline). Scan page size: a 500-entry page of the first full scan held the lock 1,993 ms, then 2,087 ms and 2,228 ms in later runs over the same 2,000 OPFS notes, above R4's 2 s target. Use a time-bounded page before folders of that size are common (the timing test only prints this number). L2A-6, Phase 4: the first list after an open from index.json stats every stored note entry in one hold (1,733 ms for 2,000 notes), and a listing that finds many new files reads them in one hold (626 ms for 300). About 2,300 stored notes or 900 new files pass the 2 s target. Bound both per hold and leave the rest to Phase 4's paged rescans and change path. Other tabs' and outside programs' edits to an existing note made after this tab compared it reach this tab's lists at its next rescan, or when this tab reads that note, until Phase 4's change messages. A note another tab's identity fix renumbered answers 404 by its new id until its old id is asked for or a rescan runs. Course delete stats every note before its detach chunks, so a note moved into the course between that pass and its chunk keeps the slug. Deferred from Phase 2 (shared content routes; design revision_log.md 12.6): Search ranking parity: the port matches CPython difflib to 1e-12 on ASCII, CJK, accented, and emoji cases, but Dart's toLowerCase and \s differ from Python's str.lower and re \s on a few code points (for example U+0130, U+001C to U+001F), and the backend scores stored content with absolute /media/ URLs where the folder has nc-folder: URLs. Heatmap edge cases: notes added by hand, adopted by a scan, or imported count on no day; the day is the device's local day, not the server's TIME_ZONE; recurring planner events are not expanded (as in the backend). Cover upload does not bump the note's last_edit (the backend does); the folder leaves the note body alone. History lists both retention pools (up to 24 versions); the backend answers 12. Chromium/OPFS: binary writes (writeBytes) of attachments, covers, and the avatar, and FolderImage reads, are tested over MemoryFolderFs only. The full-scan longest hold (2,087 ms, see "Scan page size") is unchanged by Phase 2. Editor wiring: a folder start first renders the cached cloud front page and categories from local_cache until the folder load replaces them. The client-level checks cover the passthrough, uploads, and the 503s. The regenerated doc comments of activityWeightN and the two heatmap strings now match the ARB files. Review LOW findings of loop 2a pass 2 (.agents/tasks/review-2a-pass2.json), deferred for 0.1.201: L2A2-1: the rescan replays this tab's index changes over the scan's entries without checking order, so an identity fix or another tab's save that the scan read can be reverted in the index (GET by the new id answers 404, or the list shows the older row) until a reload. Stat each logged path in the final hold and keep the entry that matches the disk; add the two-notes-same-id test. L2A2-2: purged-note summaries (title, description, excerpt) can stay in .notechondria/index.json when the tab closes within the 1 s flush delay, and a listing that drops entries schedules no flush. Write index.json at once after a purge or empty trash. L2A2-3: a journal roll-forward, and a commit that fails partway, do not update the in-memory index; this tab lists the old rows until a rescan, a read of the note, or a reload. L2A2-4: the first list after an open from index.json holds the lock 1,733 ms for 2,000 notes, and the first full scan's longest page 2,087 ms (printed only). L2A2-5 (INFO): local_folder_controller.dart is near the 1000-line cap; move the index cache (_unverified, _scanLog, _scan, _scheduleFlush, flushIndex) into its own file before it grows. Found by the 0.1.201 browser check (headless Chromium, editor in folder mode): Fonts: Flutter web loads Roboto and the Noto Sans Symbols fallback from fonts.gstatic.com (the bundle ships only MaterialIcons, CupertinoIcons, and the KaTeX fonts). With no network the first load draws no text, and folder mode still sends these font requests to Google (no note data). Bundle the fonts or set the engine's font fallback base URL to the app's own assets. Affects every mode, not only the folder. Folder-mode wording: note cards say "Synced to cloud", Settings shows "Backend settings: Online. API URL: ...", and the recycle bin page says "Cloud recycle bin" and "soft-deleted note(s) on the server". "Start empty" on an empty folder still put the browser's starter draft into the folder (the 7.1 connect-time move). By design, but the label suggests an empty folder; reword or skip the starter draft. The empty-folder step shows "Start empty" and "Cancel" only; "Start from an archive" is Phase 4. N2: _promoteQueuedAttachments deletes local blobs before the content patch; a failed patch leaves local:// URLs with no blob. N3: skip the cloud-copy draft path (draft_sync.dart:244) in folder mode; its cloud note id can name an unrelated folder note. N4: purge removes assets/notes/<hex>/ even when another note's body links to those files; document it or check references first. N5: encodeAttachments drops unknown top-level keys and records without id/filename from attachments.json. N6: search reads every body on every query (tracked as "Search hold"). 418.body: Per-user backup of all server-held text + metadata into a GitHub repository the user owns. Goal: a user can survive a complete server wipe by git clone-ing their own data back. Static assets we host (avatars, attachments, cover images) are referenced by URL; their bytes stay on our CDN and are not committed. This feature is experimental and gated behind a frontend "Experimental" card in editor settings. It is not wired into any automatic schedule; the user pushes manually for now.

419.body: Per-user install (installation_id) scoped to one repository. Tokens rotate ~hourly automatically. Revoked by the user from their GitHub settings, no server work needed on our side. Survives password rotation / 2FA changes on the user's side.

422.body: git clone the user's repo. POST /api/v1/auth/register/ (or sign in via OAuth) to recreate the Creator row. PATCH /api/v1/settings/ with mcp_skill_md, theme_*, and the app_settings blob from profile/settings.json. Recreate every course via POST /api/v1/courses/ using its slug. Recreate every note via POST /api/v1/notes/ reading the markdown body + the sidecar *.meta.json for metadata_json and custom_meta. Recreate planner events + feeds from planner/*.json. The end-to-end restore tooling is not yet shipped; 0.1.90 only covers the export half. Tracked under "Release / CI" in docs/TODO.md.

423.body: User clicks "Connect to GitHub" in editor settings → frontend redirects to GITHUB_DATA_SYNC_APP_INSTALL_URL. After install, GitHub redirects back to the editor with ?installation_id=...&setup_action=install. Frontend POSTs /api/v1/integrations/github/callback/ with the install id + chosen repo_full_name and repo_default_branch. Backend persists a GithubIntegration row keyed by Creator. User clicks "Push now" → POST /api/v1/integrations/github/push/. Backend materializes the file tree and PUTs each file via the GitHub Contents API using an installation-scoped access token.

424.body: The push and restore halves are now end-to-end functional including binary assets. The remaining work is around concurrent edits and long-term repo hygiene. Conflict resolution. The Contents API PUTs we use overwrite the remote blob. A user editing on two devices between syncs can lose changes. The next iteration should fetch the existing blob on each path, diff it against the materialized payload, and surface a "remote changed" warning before overwriting. Asset rotation / pruning. Repeated pushes with assets accumulate orphan files for notes that have been deleted client-side but whose old asset paths still live in the remote tree. A --prune-orphans mode on the push pipeline can walk the Trees API and delete unreferenced assets/notes/<uuid>/ subtrees in the same commit.

435.body: The cutover is too big for one round. Suggested phases (each its own version log): Survey + design (0.1.95 — DONE). Inventory the auth surface; ship docs/integrations/casdoor-migration.md. Casdoor SDK + JWT auth class (0.1.96 — DONE). Adds the casdoor>=1.41 Python SDK, the CasdoorJWTAuthentication DRF class (registered LAST in DEFAULT_AUTHENTICATION_CLASSES so it's a no-op until a Bearer JWT shows up that isn't an MCP key), Creator.casdoor_sub, and the public /api/v1/auth/casdoor/{config,exchange}/ endpoints. Returns 503 / {configured: false} when env vars aren't populated, so existing MultiSessionAuthentication + LoginApiView paths keep working unchanged. Frontend Casdoor SDK. Add the Flutter Casdoor package to notechondria_shared; route the existing _AuthDialog and launchOAuth paths through Casdoor's /login/oauth/authorize instead of the per-provider Google/GitHub URLs. The frontend client gains a casdoorExchange(code) method that hits the new POST /api/v1/auth/casdoor/exchange/ and reuses the existing applyAuthPayload machinery. Backend endpoints stay backwards-compatible during this phase. Cutover. Disable the legacy LoginApiView / RegisterApiView etc. endpoints; the JWT path is now the only way in. Remove MultiSessionAuthentication + Session writes; the Session model becomes read-only (populated from Casdoor session-events webhook). Cleanup. Delete every endpoint / serializer / template / helper listed above. Remove VerificationCode / InvitationCode models with a final migration. Each phase is independently shippable. Steps 2 and 3 can land in either order; both should land before step 4.
435.title: Phased migration

436.title: Phase 2 wire shape (shipped 0.1.96)

437.body: creators.casdoor_auth.CasdoorJWTAuthentication validates Authorization: Bearer <jwt> against settings.CASDOOR_CERTIFICATE (RS256). Audience must equal CASDOOR_CLIENT_ID. Bearer headers starting with ntc_ are ignored so MCP API keys keep flowing to ApiKeyAuthentication. The class is no-op when any of CASDOOR_ENDPOINT, CASDOOR_CLIENT_ID, CASDOOR_ORG_NAME, CASDOOR_APP_NAME is empty. Returns None (not AuthenticationFailed) so other classes in the chain can still handle the same header. On first valid JWT, user resolution order is: Creator.casdoor_sub == claims['id' | 'sub'] (fast path after the link is persisted). User.email iexact claims['email'] — links an existing legacy account; Creator.casdoor_sub is backfilled. Auto-provision a new User + Creator, stamp the sub. Stamps User.last_login so the existing "recently signed in" surfaces stay accurate.
437.title: Backend authentication

438.body: GET /api/v1/auth/casdoor/config/ (anon): {"configured": true, "endpoint": "https://auth.example", "client_id": "...", "organization": "...", "application": "...", "signin_url": "https://auth.example/login/oauth/authorize"} When unconfigured: {"configured": false} with no other fields, so the SPA can keep showing the legacy auth surface. POST /api/v1/auth/casdoor/exchange/ (anon): Request: {"code": "<casdoor-authz-code>", "state": "..."}. Response (200): the standard auth_payload shape used by LoginApiView — token + session + user + app_settings. Response (503): {detail: "...shadow mode..."} when the SDK isn't configured.

440.body: The phase-2 exchange endpoint resolves identity automatically via Creator.casdoor_sub → email-iexact → auto-provision. The bind/unlink path covers two cases the auto-resolve can't: The Casdoor email differs from the Notechondria email, so the email-iexact branch can't find the legacy account. The user wants to deliberately disconnect a previously linked Casdoor identity without losing access (the legacy session keeps working).

441.body: POST /api/v1/auth/casdoor/bind/ (auth required): Request: {"code": "<casdoor-authz-code>"}. Backend exchanges via get_oauth_token, verifies the JWT, takes the sub, and: Returns 409 if the same sub is already on a different Creator (the user must unlink that side first). Otherwise persists Creator.casdoor_sub for the current user and returns the standard auth_payload. DELETE /api/v1/auth/casdoor/unlink/ (auth required): Idempotent. Clears Creator.casdoor_sub. Returns {"casdoor_linked": false, "was_linked": <bool>}. Does NOT log the user out — the existing legacy Session keeps working.
441.title: Endpoints

442.body: Settings GET response now includes casdoor_linked: bool so the Connected Accounts UI can render the right state without an extra round-trip.
442.title: Settings surface

443.body: AuthClient gains casdoorBind(token, code) + casdoorUnlink(token). Each app's client implements them. AppShellOAuthMixin.handleOAuthCallback dispatches the state=casdoor branch on intent: 'login' → exchange, 'bind' → bind. The bind branch refuses to fall through to the legacy provider login when the session token is missing. All three apps' _ConnectedAccountsSection widgets gain a Casdoor SSO row with Link / Unlink controls; onBindCasdoor and onUnlinkCasdoor are constructed in each app shell when _casdoorConfigured && _token != null.

444.body: Username migration. Casdoor users are keyed by an opaque name (Casdoor) plus an id (UUID). The mapping table from existing auth_user.username to Casdoor name must be pre-populated before cutover or first-login users will end up duplicated. Resolved (cutover round): the management command python manage.py migrate_users_to_casdoor walks auth_user.is_active=True, calls CasdoorSDK.get_user_by_email to deduplicate, then add_user / update_user for each row, and finally stamps Creator.casdoor_sub so the next JWT login takes the fast path. Idempotent; supports --dry-run, --retry-existing, --strict, and --limit N for staged rollout. Linked SocialAccount rows are pushed into Casdoor's per-provider fields (user.google, user.github) so prior OAuth identities resolve to the same Casdoor row. MCP API keys. The ntc_<32-hex> Bearer scheme stays app-internal; Casdoor is not used for the MCP per-request hot path. The /api/v1/auth/rotate-api-key/ endpoint stays. OAuth redirect-allow-list. Casdoor handles per-app redirect_uri allow-lists centrally. The GOOGLE_AUTHORIZED_REDIRECT_URIS / GITHUB_AUTHORIZED_REDIRECT_URIS env vars added in 0.1.90 become unused once cutover lands. Email verification copy. Casdoor's templated email is generic; if we want the Notechondria-branded email body, we need to ship a Casdoor email template via its admin API as part of the migration.

446.body: Proposal to move the Model Context Protocol (MCP) server out of the Django backend and into a standalone CLI app that talks to the backend over the public /api/v1/ HTTP surface. Written at 0.1.135. Status: Phases 1–3 done (through 0.1.146) — the audit confirmed every MCP tool maps to /api/v1/ (one missing note-sessions GET added in 0.1.146), and the CLI in cli/ now implements all 41 tools at parity with backend/mcp/tools.py. The in-backend /mcp/ endpoint keeps working unchanged. Remaining: Phase 4 (PyPI) + Phase 5 (deferred cutover).
446.breadcrumbs: MCP → CLI migration proposal » MCP → standalone CLI migration proposal
446.title: MCP → standalone CLI migration proposal

447.body: Keep both. /mcp/ (HTTP, in-backend) and the CLI (stdio) both stay — separate endpoints/transports, shared authentication (the ntc_ API key). One API key per user (already the case — Creator.api_key_hash is a single field). Location: the CLI lives in this repo's cli/ directory for now but is an independent program (own pyproject.toml, no imports from backend/); it may move to its own repo later. Language: Python . Cadence: keep /mcp/ until further notice (no cutover/deletion yet). Parity rule (agent-oriented development): every new tool or behavior is implemented in both backend/mcp/tools.py and cli/notechondria_mcp/tools.py. The two servers must stay interchangeable.
447.breadcrumbs: MCP → CLI migration proposal » Owner decisions (locked 0.1.138)
447.title: Owner decisions (locked 0.1.138)

448.body: Today MCP lives inside the Django backend ( backend/mcp/ ): a single POST /mcp/ JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint, authenticated with Bearer ntc_<key> ( creators/authentication.py ), exposing ~44 tools ( backend/mcp/tools.py ) that call the Django ORM directly (the tool handlers import notes/courses/planner models and services, not the HTTP API). Problems with keeping it in the backend: Tight coupling. Every tool is bound to the ORM, so the MCP surface can only run where the full Django app + database + secrets run. It cannot be distributed to a user's machine. Deployment weight. Agents that want MCP must reach the production backend's /mcp/ route; there is no local/offline or self-hosted-against-someone-else's-backend story. Coupled release cadence. MCP tool changes ship on the backend release train even though the protocol layer is independent of the business logic. Doc drift. docs/server/mcp.md already describes a stale auth header (ApiKey nch_live_…) vs the real Bearer ntc_…, and an outdated tool count — a symptom of the protocol layer and the API surface living in one place but evolving at different speeds. The backend already exposes a versioned /api/v1/ REST surface that covers the same operations the MCP tools perform. That makes a clean split possible: the backend stays the source of truth and the API; the MCP protocol layer becomes a thin client.
448.breadcrumbs: MCP → CLI migration proposal » 1. Why move it
448.title: 1. Why move it

449.body:
┌──────────────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────────────┐
│ notechondria-mcp (CLI app) │ │ Notechondria backend (Django)│
│ │ │ │
│ MCP server (stdio / HTTP) │ │ /api/v1/* REST surface │
│ initialize / tools.list / │ HTTPS │ ApiKeyAuthentication │
│ tools.call │ ─────► │ (Bearer ntc_<key>) │
│ │ ntc_ │ │
│ Tool handlers → API calls │ key │ ORM, business logic, │
│ Config (~/.notechondria/) │ │ storage, skill.md │
└──────────────────────────────┘ └──────────────────────────────┘ Transport. Use the official MCP SDK so the protocol/transport (stdio for desktop agent integration, optionally Streamable HTTP) is not hand-rolled. Python mcp package or TypeScript @modelcontextprotocol/sdk. Recommended: Python , to match the backend stack and reuse request/serialization idioms. Tool handlers map each MCP tool call to one or more /api/v1/... requests with the Authorization: Bearer ntc_<key> header, then format the JSON response into MCP content. Config lives in ~/.notechondria/config.json (or NOTECHONDRIA_API_KEY + NOTECHONDRIA_API_URL env vars): the backend base URL and the ntc_ key.

The CLI sends it as Bearer ntc_<key> on every /api/v1/ call; the backend validates it exactly as /mcp/ does today. No new identity surface, no OAuth in the CLI.

453.body: Small and additive — none breaks the existing /mcp/ endpoint: Expose mcp_skill_md over the API. Today it is only readable via the MCP initialize response. Add GET /api/v1/auth/mcp-skill/ (returns {"mcp_skill_md": "..."}) so the CLI can fetch it on startup. (Or include it in the existing settings GET payload.) Confirm /api/v1/ covers every MCP tool operation. Audit the ~44 tools against the REST surface ( docs/api/backend_api_spec.md ); add endpoints for any tool that currently reaches into the ORM with no HTTP equivalent (e.g. note-version snapshot/restore, note sessions, heatmap/activity-week payloads — confirm each has a /api/v1/ route). CORS / headers. Already handled by ApiCorsMiddleware for /api/v1/; verify the CLI's requests (server-to-server, no browser) are unaffected — they will be, since CORS is a browser concern. API stability. Treat /api/v1/ as a stable public contract for the CLI; version-lock per release (already the convention). No database migration is needed.

453.title: 4. Backend changes required

454.body: Each phase is independently shippable; the in-backend /mcp/ stays live until the final cutover. Phase 1 — API gap audit (DONE, 0.1.145–0.1.146). Mapped all 41 MCP tools to /api/v1/. Every tool had a REST equivalent except list_note_sessions (the note-sessions/ view was POST-only); a filtered GET was added + tested in 0.1.146. Doc corrected in docs/server/mcp.md (auth header, 41-tool list, coverage table). Backend-only, fully tested. No MCP-protocol change. Phase 2 — CLI skeleton (DONE, 0.1.138). notechondria-mcp in cli/ : config loading (env / ~/.notechondria/ config.json), a requests-based backend client, a stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 server (initialize fetching skill.md, tools/list, tools/call, ping), and a representative tool subset (notes CRUD, courses, planner events) calling /api/v1/. Unit-tested without network or an MCP SDK (python -m unittest discover tests). The transport is hand-rolled for now (no SDK dependency); it can adopt the official Python mcp SDK later without changing the tool layer. Phase 3 — full tool parity (DONE, 0.1.146). All 41 tools from backend/mcp/tools.py are now implemented in cli/notechondria_mcp/tools.py with matching names + input schemas, so connected agents see no behavior change between servers. A name-set diff (backend vs CLI) is asserted identical; CLI dispatch is unit-tested without network. (Per the parity rule, future tools land in both servers together.) Phase 4 — distribute. Publish to PyPI (pip install notechondria-mcp) with a notechondria-mcp entry point; document the agent-side config (stdio command + env). Optionally ship a PyInstaller binary on GitHub Releases for non-Python users. Phase 5 — cutover + cleanup. Point the docs and Settings UI at the CLI; keep /mcp/ for one deprecation window, then delete backend/mcp/ (the app, urls, tests) and drop the mcp capability from the handshake.
454.breadcrumbs: MCP → CLI migration proposal » 5. Phased plan
454.title: 5. Phased plan

455.body: Latency. Each tool call becomes 1+ HTTP round-trips to the backend instead of a local ORM query. For an interactive agent this is negligible; batch-heavy tools may need a /api/v1/ bulk endpoint. Two codebases. The CLI and backend evolve separately; mitigated by treating /api/v1/ as a versioned contract and sharing the tool schemas via the API spec doc. Distribution surface. A pip package is a new artifact to release and secure; offset by decoupling MCP from the backend deploy.
455.title: 6. Trade-offs

459.body: The adapter was run against the real Veronica-7 tree (211 blobs, 195 markdown files) — read-only, no fork, no writes — reproducing production behaviour by feeding it the GitHub tree API's path list (which, unlike a local glob, includes dotfiles such as docs/.vitepress/): infer_preset → vitepress (detects docs/.vitepress/config.mts). .vitepress/** and public/** are excluded; repo-root README.md / TODO.md never leak in (content root is docs). module_depth: 1 → 6 modules, all 193 course notes, 0 warnings : cv → "Modern CV — Overview", dnn → "Deep Neural Networks", fundamentals → "Fundamentals & History", llm → "Large Language Models", transformer-era → "The Transformer Era", plus the landing pages (docs/index.md, docs/about.md, docs/templates.md). module_depth: 2 → 37 fine-grained modules (e.g. cv/advances, dnn/rl, transformer-era/2023-2024). Frontmatter (title, order, …) round-trips through compose_markdown, so a later sync re-emits it and doesn't disturb the site's rendering. Result: no adapter bug. Depth 1 is the recommended grouping (clean, index-titled modules that mirror the VitePress sidebars).

The Notechondria backend verifies inbound JWTs against this PEM. Back on the Applications → notechondria screen, set the Cert field to notechondria-cert.

467.body: Casdoor's redirect-URI allow-list is centralised on the application. Each Flutter frontend lives at a different origin, so add one entry per app : App Redirect URI Editor https://trance-0.github.io/Notechondria/editor/ Planner https://trance-0.github.io/Notechondria/planner/ Portal https://trance-0.github.io/Notechondria/portal/ For local dev add the localhost equivalents too: App Redirect URI Editor http://localhost:8001/ Planner http://localhost:8002/ Portal http://localhost:8003/ (The exact ports depend on what flutter run -d chrome picks for each app — pin them via --web-port if you want stable values.) The Notechondria backend computes the redirect_uri from the caller's Origin header per the launchOAuth('casdoor', ...) flow, so each app's outbound authorization URL ends with the matching origin. Any URI not on Casdoor's allow-list above will be rejected with a redirect_uri mismatch error.

469.body:
Drop these into the backend .env (or the deployment-method equivalent — see deploy.md , render_free_tier.md , northflank.md ): CASDOOR_ENDPOINT=https://auth.trance-0.com
CASDOOR_CLIENT_ID=<from the application "Client ID" field>
CASDOOR_CLIENT_SECRET=<from the application "Client secret" field>
CASDOOR_ORG_NAME=notechondria
CASDOOR_APP_NAME=notechondria
CASDOOR_CERTIFICATE=<single-line PEM with literal \n escapes>
# Optional: how long to cache JWT-verification results in seconds
# (default 300). The verifier itself is stateless; this just
# amortises the cert-parsing cost when the same token shows up
# again within the window.
CASDOOR_TOKEN_CACHE_TTL=300 CASDOOR_CERTIFICATE is the public-key PEM you downloaded in §1c. The newline-to-\n escape is so the PEM survives a single-line shell .env. _normalize_pem in backend/creators/casdoor_auth.py converts the escaped form back to multi-line at signing time. Same trick used by the GitHub data-sync app's private key. When any of the first four are empty, every Casdoor surface on the backend is a no-op (auth class returns None, exchange endpoint returns 503, config endpoint returns {configured: false}). That's the shadow mode the migration plan calls out — safe default until you're ready to flip the switch.

# "signin_url": "https://auth.trance-0.com/login/oauth/authorize"} Hit /api/v1/handshake/ and confirm version matches the deployed VERSION file (this surface was fixed in 0.1.95 — if it returns "0.0.0" your container didn't ship VERSION to /home/VERSION). On the frontend: Open any of the three apps. Sign-out. The Account card should now lead with a full-width "Continue with Casdoor SSO" button (since 0.1.99). Legacy email / password sits behind the "Use email / password instead" expander. Click the SSO button → redirects to https://auth.trance-0.com/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=…&state=casdoor&.... Casdoor authenticates → redirects back with ?code=.... Frontend calls POST /api/v1/auth/casdoor/exchange/ automatically; the SPA ends up signed in the same way as the legacy login flow. Inspect Settings → Connected accounts — the Casdoor row shows "Linked". For the bind path (link Casdoor to an existing legacy account when the emails differ): sign in legacy first, then in Settings → Connected accounts click Link Casdoor on the Casdoor row. Casdoor is opened with state=casdoor + intent=bind; the callback hits POST /api/v1/auth/casdoor/bind/ with the existing session token, and the link is recorded on Creator.casdoor_sub. The legacy session keeps working.

472.body: After a successful Casdoor sign-in: Creator.casdoor_sub (TextField on backend/creators/models.py) holds the Casdoor user id / sub claim. Used as the fast-path key on subsequent JWT verifies. creators.Session row is still minted by auth_payload(user, request) so the existing MultiSessionAuthentication keeps working — the SPA uses the same Authorization: Token <session-key> header it always did. Casdoor JWTs are only used at sign-in time; the per- request hot path stays on the legacy session token until the phase-4 cutover. Once cutover lands, Session becomes a read-only audit table populated from Casdoor session-events webhooks; the per-request hot path moves entirely onto JWT verification by CasdoorJWTAuthentication.
