473.body:
Casdoor's Application > Token > Token Format tab lets you emit arbitrary custom JWT claims. The default Notechondria backend reads id / sub, email, name, firstName, lastName — the historical Casdoor shape. To match a Nextcloud-style attribute mapping, configure the backend env to read whichever claim names Casdoor emits. The pattern is identical to the Nextcloud user_oidc plugin's claim mapping. Recommended Token Format mapping in the Casdoor admin UI (matches the user_oidc convention): JWT claim Casdoor source Type preferred_username Name String name DisplayName String email Email String groups Groups Array Then in the backend env (Northflank service env or linked Secret Group), set: CASDOOR_CLAIM_USERNAME=preferred_username,name
CASDOOR_CLAIM_DISPLAY_NAME=name,displayName
CASDOOR_CLAIM_EMAIL=email
CASDOOR_CLAIM_GROUPS=groups Each value is a comma-separated list of claim names tried in order — the first non-empty wins. Defaults preserve historical 0.1.96 behavior, so leaving these unset keeps the existing auto-provision flow working.
473.breadcrumbs: Casdoor login setup runbook » 6. JWT claim mapping + group ACL (since 0.1.110)
473.title: 6. JWT claim mapping + group ACL (since 0.1.110)

474.body:
CASDOOR_REQUIRED_GROUPS is a comma-separated list of group names; the JWT's groups claim (read via CASDOOR_CLAIM_GROUPS) must contain at least one match for the JWT to authenticate. Empty (default) disables gating — any verified Casdoor JWT is accepted. # Only let members of the app-notechondria group sign in.
# Casdoor typically emits org-scoped groups as `<org>/<group>`,
# so list the full path as it appears in the JWT.
CASDOOR_REQUIRED_GROUPS=notechondria/app-notechondria Match is exact and case-sensitive. When a sign-in is denied, the backend logs a warning at Backend.Creators.CasdoorAuth/authenticate with the reason, and the frontend's auth-failure SnackBar surfaces a precise message ("Cannot sign in: ... — user is not a member of any required group (...)"). This mirrors the Nextcloud user_oidc plugin's "Restrict login to a list of groups" toggle. Group membership itself is managed in Casdoor under Identity > Groups and assigned to users via Identity > Users > <user> > Edit. There is no Notechondria-side group management — group state lives entirely in Casdoor and the backend just gates on it.

474.title: Group-based access control

475.body: The /api/v1/auth/casdoor/config/ endpoint and the entire CasdoorJWTAuthentication class are gated by the deployed backend image. If curl https://<backend>/api/v1/auth/casdoor/config/ returns 404 even after setting all the env vars, the deployed image predates 0.1.96 — redeploy on Northflank (or whichever host is in use) to pick up the routes. The frontend boot probe writes a warning to Editor.Auth/casdoor.config.probe with the full URL it tried, so the operator can grep the log for the exact backend that's stale.

476.body: 0.1.119 added a per-login profile refresh: every authenticated request runs _sync_creator_from_claims(creator, claims) which copies the JWT's profile attributes onto the local Creator row. The fields synced are: JWT claim Notechondria attribute Notes displayName Creator.display_name preferred over username on public surfaces avatar Creator.avatar_url remote URL; preferred over the locally-uploaded Creator.image firstName User.first_name lastName User.last_name email User.email Notechondria deliberately never writes back to User.username. Username is the stable PK reference shape — changing it would break every owner-keyed FK on courses, notes, attachments, plus external links to /api/v1/creators/<username>/. Casdoor's username can be edited freely; Notechondria's local username only gets set once at account creation (either through the bind path against an existing legacy account, or through the create-with-password path off the gitea-style link challenge in 0.1.118). The sync is throttled to 5-minute granularity via Creator.casdoor_profile_synced_at — a busy SPA fires hundreds of JWT-authenticated requests during a session and we don't want each one writing to the DB. Within 5 minutes of the last sync, the helper is a no-op.
476.breadcrumbs: Casdoor login setup runbook » 7. Profile-sync custom JWT field (since 0.1.119)
476.title: 7. Profile-sync custom JWT field (since 0.1.119)

477.body:
Casdoor doesn't emit avatar by default; you have to add it explicitly under the application's Token tab. Steps: Casdoor admin UI → Identity > Applications > notechondria . Open the Token sub-tab. Scroll to Custom JWT fields and click Add . Fill in: Name : avatar Category : Existing Field Value : Avatar (the user-record's avatar URL field; Casdoor stores avatars at <endpoint>/files/avatar/<org>/<user>.png) Type : String Save the application. After this, Casdoor's emitted JWT will include avatar like: { "sub": "<uuid>", "displayName": "ncadmin", "avatar": "https://auth.trance-0.com/files/avatar/notechondria/Trance-0.png", "email": "user@example.com", "firstName": "", "lastName": "", "groups": ["trance-0/app-notechondria", ...]
} The default Notechondria env var CASDOOR_CLAIM_AVATAR=avatar already points at that claim, so no further config is needed when the Casdoor side names the field avatar exactly. Override via CASDOOR_CLAIM_AVATAR=picture (or any comma-separated list) if your Casdoor instance emits a different name — following the same pattern as the other CASDOOR_CLAIM_* mappings from §6.

478.body: For a setup that maps cleanly onto Notechondria's profile refresh, the application's Token > Custom JWT fields should look like (the user-supplied JWT example for auth.trance-0.com matches this shape): Name Category Value Type preferred_username Existing Field Name String displayName Existing Field DisplayName String email Existing Field Email String avatar Existing Field Avatar String groups Existing Field Groups Array firstName / lastName are part of Casdoor's standard JWT shape and don't need a custom-fields entry. sub is Casdoor's internal UUID — never edit it.

479.body: When a user signs into Casdoor, edits their display name in the Casdoor user portal at <endpoint>/account/<orgname>/<username>, and then opens any Notechondria SPA tab: The SPA's stored Casdoor JWT triggers CasdoorJWTAuthentication.authenticate on the next authenticated request. JWT verifies, group ACL passes, user resolves via Creator.casdoor_sub. _sync_creator_from_claims(creator, claims) runs — throttled to 5 minutes, but the user's edit is fresh enough to push Creator.display_name / Creator.avatar_url / User.first_name etc. to whatever Casdoor now reports. The next page that reads auth_payload (or /api/v1/settings/) sees the updated display_name and image_url fields and re-renders the avatar / byline. No frontend code change is required — the SPA already prefers the backend's image_url over the local avatar_url field explicitly when the backend resolves the priority chain server-side (see auth_payload in creators/api.py).

490.body: The repo root scripts/ directory includes four click-run Python scripts for operator backups. Each script reads credentials directly from the repo-root .env file and does not require command-line arguments.
490.breadcrumbs: Local Backup and Restore Scripts » Local Backup and Restore Scripts
490.title: Local Backup and Restore Scripts

491.body: scripts/backup_database.py scripts/restore_database.py The database backup script writes a PostgreSQL tar-format dump to: scripts/db_backup/<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>.tar The restore script uses the newest .tar in scripts/db_backup/ unless RESTORE_FILE is set inside the script. Both scripts read DATABASE_URL first. If that is absent, they build a connection string from: POSTGRE_HOST POSTGRE_PORT POSTGRE_DB POSTGRE_USERNAME POSTGRE_PASSWORD The database scripts require PostgreSQL client tools on the local machine: pg_dump pg_restore
491.breadcrumbs: Local Backup and Restore Scripts » Database
491.title: Database

492.body: scripts/backup_cloudflare_r2.py scripts/restore_cloudflare_r2.py The R2 backup script writes an app-version-independent tar archive to: scripts/r2_backup/<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>.tar The archive contains manifest.json plus opaque object payloads under objects/. The manifest maps each object key to its payload path and records content type, size, ETag, and last-modified values where R2 returns them. The R2 scripts read: CLOUDFLARE_R2_BUCKET_NAME CLOUDFLARE_R2_ACCOUNT_ID CLOUDFLARE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID CLOUDFLARE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY They use Python stdlib AWS SigV4 signing against Cloudflare's S3 API, so boto3 and AWS CLI are not required.
492.breadcrumbs: Local Backup and Restore Scripts » Cloudflare R2
492.title: Cloudflare R2

493.body: Each script has editable constants near the top: USER_SELECTED_BACKUP_DIR: use a custom backup directory. BACKUP_FILENAME: force a backup filename. RESTORE_FILE: restore an exact archive instead of the newest one. REQUIRE_CONFIRMATION: restore safety prompt. The R2 restore script also has: DELETE_REMOTE_OBJECTS_NOT_IN_BACKUP: when False, restore overwrites matching keys and leaves extra remote objects alone. Set to True only when intentionally replacing the bucket contents with the archive state. Do not commit generated backup archives. They contain production data and may include user media.

504.body: Planner and portal, Settings, signed out: "Use a local folder (no account)" with the "Remember this folder on this browser" checkbox, the same option the editor shows. On desktop Chromium browsers (Chrome, Edge) over https or http://127.0.0.1, the chosen folder becomes the app's storage. Planner events with their completion state are in planner/events.json; imported calendars are in planner/feeds.json, with the calendar text in planner/feeds/<id>.ics. Courses, planner events, and imported calendars the browser stored before the folder was chosen move into the folder once, when it is connected. The browser keeps recovery copies for 30 days. In the portal, a link to a folder note (#/note/<uuid>) opens the folder first and then the note. While the folder waits for a pick or a permission, the page shows the reconnect view. 509.body: Editor, Settings, signed out: a new "Use a local folder (no account)" button under the sign-in buttons, with a "Remember this folder on this browser" checkbox. On desktop Chromium browsers (Chrome, Edge) over https or http://127.0.0.1, the button opens the folder picker. The chosen folder becomes the editor's storage: notes are Markdown files under notes/ with a .meta.json sidecar, and categories, trash, version history, snapshots, attachments, covers, the avatar, writing sessions, search, the front page, and the heatmap are files in the same folder. The page answers every API call itself, so no note data goes to the Notechondria server. The one exception is "Check for updates", which asks the saved server for its version and sends no token. Notes the browser had stored locally move into the folder when it is connected. The browser keeps recoverable copies in its local recycle bin for 30 days. With "Remember this folder" checked, a reload reopens the folder. When the browser drops the folder permission, a reconnect view replaces the editor until the user grants it again. Firefox, Safari, mobile browsers, and plain http pages show the button disabled with the reason, for example: "Local folder mode unavailable: Shared.LocalFolder/qualify — this browser does not provide window.showDirectoryPicker (File System Access API). 525.body: AppShellLogMixin.startupStep writes a DEBUG "started" record and the outcome with its duration for each step: local_state, config, handshake, session_restore, oauth_callback, initial_data (<App>.Startup/<step>). A failing step logs <consequence>: <App>.Startup/<step> — <cause> and rethrows. describeRequestFailure (notechondria_shared/lib/src/startup/startup_log.dart) names the cause (timeout after 10s (server did not respond), connection refused, DNS lookup failed, the browser's opaque network error, HTML instead of JSON (HTTP 502), ...), drops query strings, and redacts Token / Bearer values. send logs HTTP request failed: <App>.HTTP/request_failed — GET <host><path> after <n>ms: <cause>. and <App>.HTTP/slow for startup requests of 3s or more. A non-JSON body is logged and thrown as Server response not usable: <App>.HTTP/response — expected JSON from GET <url> but received HTML (HTTP 502, text/html, <n>B); check the API base URL and backend routing. verifyHandshake goes through send and, inside a startup pass, is bounded only by the shared 10s budget. Its result also answers the version banner's first probe, so startup sends one handshake. config records the API base and why it was chosen; session_restore records no saved session / saved session validated / kept / cleared: <cause> (the clearing behavior is unchanged). No tokens, cookies, passwords, or profile data are logged. initial_data reports its real outcome: _loadInitialData falls back to local data instead of throwing, so after a fallback the step logs WARNING Startup finished on local data only: <App>.Startup/initial_data — <cause>. instead of done. Startup records written before the persisted log is loaded are kept, and the log is not saved until that merge, so startup never overwrites the stored history. The merge runs right after the store load, before anything else in _loadLocalState can throw. If the store load itself throws, _handleBootstrapFailure reads the stored log on its own (_LocalAppStore.loadLogs) and merges it, so a failed start and every Retry still persist their lines. The API-base check in Settings now says API base not changed: <App>.Sync.Settings/save — handshake with <url> failed: <cause>. (it was Backend handshake failed for <url>: <cause>, with no module/process).

532.body: Bounded startup requests (notechondria_shared/lib/src/startup/startup_budget.dart). Cold start (session restore, OAuth exchange, initial data, deep links), the banner's Retry, and its Work offline run inside a StartupRequestBudget. HttpClientInternalsMixin.send enforces it: each request gets 10s, and the first timeout fails the remaining requests of that pass immediately. An unresponsive backend therefore ends in the banner after about 10s instead of an empty shell that never finishes loading. Requests started from user actions outside these passes (uploads, GitHub push) keep their previous, unbounded behavior. A startup timeout no longer clears the saved session. Bootstrap failure screen (StartupFailureView). Global guards (runGuardedApp in each main.dart): runZonedGuarded, PlatformDispatcher.instance.onError, a chained FlutterError.onError, and a non-blank ErrorWidget.builder (StartupErrorWidget). An uncaught error before the first frame swaps in a minimal fallback app with Retry. 540.body: Server side was fully healthy — every asset (fonts, FontManifest.json, CanvasKit .wasm, both manifests) returned 200 with correct sizes, and the backend answered boot endpoints in <1s. The failure was client-side and Firefox-visible , the signature of a stale / looping service worker : This Flutter SDK deprecated its service worker and ships a 784-byte self-destroying flutter_service_worker.js (the bootstrap even carries the "service worker is deprecated" notice), yet flutter_bootstrap.js still registered it on every load . A browser could get caught re-registering/unregistering that worker, serving a broken cached asset mix (→ the font NS_ERROR) and never painting. The smoke test never sees this: it runs in the Flutter test VM with no service worker and empty storage, so it kept passing while real browsers hung. (All three apps ship the same worker; portal was simply the one being used.)

541.body: Enabled the repo's own STRIP_SERVICE_WORKER kill switch (Actions variable → true) and hardened the strip step in frontend-pages.yml: Remove the serviceWorkerSettings key from _flutter.loader.load(…) — now matching both the inline-object and minified-variable forms (the old regex only matched the inline form, so it silently no-op'd on the current SDK). A build-time assert fails loudly if the key ever survives, so this can't regress silently again. Keep a self-destroying flutter_service_worker.js at the registered URL (the old switch deleted it). A browser still holding a stale worker now updates to it on the next navigation, unregisters, and reloads once — rather than 404-ing on update and staying broken. Net effect: no service worker is registered going forward (every load fetches fresh), and already-stuck browsers self-heal on their next visit. Offline PWA caching is not lost — the deprecated self-destroying worker never cached anything anyway.

547.body: Fixes #28. Repeated include_assets=true pushes accumulate orphan files: when a note is deleted client-side, its assets/notes/<uuid>/… subtree keeps living in the remote tree (the push builds a delta on base_tree, so it only ever adds/updates — it never removed the dead paths).

548.body: _orphan_asset_deletions(remote_tree, live_asset_uuids) — a pure helper that, given the recursive remote tree and the set of live note uuid hexes, returns Git-tree delete entries (sha=None, the Trees API delete form) for every assets/notes/<uuid>/… blob whose uuid is not live. Only note-asset blobs are ever targeted — notes, course files, the profile export, the avatar, and any hand-added repo files are never touched; tree entries are never emitted. commit_and_push(..., prune_asset_uuids=None) — when the set is supplied, it fetches the recursive base tree and appends the orphan deletions to the same tree POST, so pruning lands in the same atomic commit as the push (no extra commit, no separate round-trip). If the remote tree is truncated (very large repo), pruning is skipped and logged rather than acting on a partial listing. push_user_data(..., prune_orphans=False) — computes the live set as the creator's current, non-soft-deleted notes (exactly what the export materializes) and passes it down. POST /api/v1/creators/github/sync/push/ accepts a prune_orphans flag (query string or JSON body, same truthy parsing as include_assets/force) and echoes it in the response. Defaults to false, so existing callers are unchanged.

Each deletion is asserted to be a null-sha blob entry. 551.body: POST /api/v1/courses/<id>/transfer/ (CourseTransferApiView, owner-only). Body: {"target": "<username or email>"} (also accepts username / email). Case-insensitive lookup. 403 if the requester doesn't own the course, 401 if anonymous. 404 if no user matches the target; 400 if the target is the current owner or no target was given. 409 if the recipient already has a category with the same title (titles are case-insensitively unique per creator — mirrors the PATCH guard) so the owner renames first rather than creating a collision. On success: reassigns Course.creator_id; notes keep their own creator_id (co-authored notes stay with their authors); client_course_id is dropped (it was the old owner's device-local id and would collide with the recipient's unique key); and the GitHub binding is cleared because it points at the previous owner's repo, which the recipient cannot push to. The response echoes git_binding_cleared. Wrapped in a transaction; audit-logged. Tests: courses.tests.CourseTransferApiTests — transfer by username/email (case-insensitive), notes keep their author, git binding cleared, non-owner 403, unknown target 404, self 400, missing target 400, title collision 409, anonymous rejected.

554.body: Fixes #13. Local drafts, courses, and events live in the browser's storage for an origin , which every user who signs in on that device shares. Before this change nothing stamped an owner on that data, so on a shared machine user B could sign in where user A had worked offline, see A's drafts, and push them into B's cloud account — a cross-user data leak.
554.breadcrumbs: 0.1.192 - Offline cache is owner-scoped (no cross-user leak) » 0.1.192 - Offline cache is owner-scoped (no cross-user leak)
554.title: 0.1.192 - Offline cache is owner-scoped (no cross-user leak)

555.body: Ownership decision (local_data_ownership.dart, shared). A pure resolveLocalDataOwner({recordedOwner, currentUser}) returns claimed (no stamp yet → the current user claims the local data), sameUser (stamp matches — normal case, case/space-insensitive), or foreignUser (stamp belongs to someone else). It is a pure function so it can be unit-tested in CI (see below). Reconcile at sign-in (app_shell_session_mixin.dart, shared). applyAuthPayload now calls _reconcileLocalDataOwner right after the session persists: claimed/sameUser → record local_data_owner and clear any foreign_local_data_owner flag. foreignUser → set foreign_local_data_owner to the prior owner, log a warning, and show the person signing in a heads-up. The stamp is not reassigned — retagging would let the other user's cache sync as the new user's. No auto-push of a stranger's data. The post-login auto-sync (syncAllLocalCourses + syncAllLocalDrafts) is now skipped when the device's cache is foreign. _reconcileLocalDataOwner returns that flag so the caller can gate the push. Manual sync refuses too (all 3 apps). _syncAllLocalData in the editor, planner, and portal returns an error (and messages the user) when foreign_local_data_owner is set, so the "sync local data" button can't push a stranger's drafts either. Escape hatch. The warning tells the user to clear local data (Settings) or sign in as the prior owner to keep the offline notes. Clearing local data resets the stamp via _LocalAppStore.defaultSettings, so the next sign-in claims the (now empty) storage cleanly. The ownership keys ride the existing applyLocalAppSettings → _applyLocalAppSettings (spread-merge) → saveSettings (whole-map jsonEncode) path, so they persist across reloads like any other local setting.

The shared package's own test/ is not CI-run and there is no local Flutter SDK, so the security-critical decision was pushed into a pure function a CI-run app test can exercise. 564.breadcrumbs: 0.1.189 - GitHub sync: no more silent overwrites (atomic push + conflict gate) » 0.1.189 - GitHub sync: no more silent overwrites (atomic push + conflict gate)
564.title: 0.1.189 - GitHub sync: no more silent overwrites (atomic push + conflict gate)

565.body: github_sync.commit_and_push walked the file list and issued one Contents API PUT per path, each overwriting the remote blob with a sha read moments earlier. Two consequences: Silent data loss. Anything committed since the previous sync — a second device, or an edit made directly on GitHub — was discarded with no warning. Non-atomic and slow. One request per file meant a partial push if anything failed mid-loop, and N sequential round-trips (the same pathology fixed for course sync in 0.1.176; profile sync never got the treatment). Rewritten to a single Git Data API commit — blobs → tree on base_tree → commit → ref update — with a conflict gate : the branch head is compared against GithubIntegration.last_push_sha, and if the remote moved, the push raises GithubSyncConflict instead of overwriting . A blank last_push_sha (first-ever push) has nothing to compare and proceeds. POST integrations/github/push/ returns 409 with {"conflict": true} and an explanatory message, rather than a generic 400 — the request was valid; the world moved. ?force=1 (or {"force": true}) is the deliberate overwrite path, threaded through push_user_data(force=…). Blobs are uploaded base64 and referenced by sha, so attachment bytes survive intact (inline tree content would be UTF-8 only). A tree identical to the published one produces no commit at all .

588.body: Live-debugged with the owner's API credentials: auth.trance-0.com serves avatar files without any CORS headers , while our media CDN (cdn.trance-0.com) sends access-control-allow-origin correctly. Flutter web's renderer refuses to draw cross-origin images without CORS — so every avatar pointing at Casdoor could never render, regardless of frontend fallback chains. Fix (as specified by the owner): store the avatar into our storage at authentication. Creator.avatar_mirrored_from (migration 0036) records the source URL of the last mirror. creators.utils.mirror_remote_avatar(creator) downloads the Casdoor avatar (8 s timeout, image content-types only, 8 MB cap) into Creator.image (→ R2). Idempotent per avatar change; best-effort so a slow IdP never blocks login. Called from the Casdoor claims sync on every login. Payloads (auth_payload, settings serializer, creator_summary_payload): image_url — the effective avatar — now points at the mirrored copy when fresh (CORS-safe); avatar_url stays the raw Casdoor URL for reference/fallback. Frontend bylines (portal + editor) flipped to image_url first with avatar_url as fallback. Note: existing accounts heal on their next Casdoor login (that's when the mirror runs).

Every page reload signed the user out silently, which surfaced as: no login info shown (#7), no subscribed courses in the course list (#6), an empty course list feeding the activity filter → no category dropdown (#2), and "new project missing" (#8: courses created while effectively signed out were device-local to one app). 62.body: The editor's compatibility target is a boring folder format that can be read without Notechondria: journal/ 2026/ 2026-05-22/ entry.md metadata.json media/ IMG_001.heic voice.m4a entry.md renders as GitHub-flavored Markdown. Metadata belongs in YAML frontmatter and/or metadata.json so geodata, place names, weather, mood, tags, source app, media pointers, created/updated timestamps, and sync provenance remain structured instead of buried in prose. The format can support modern post/blog structure beyond simple Markdown, but should avoid opaque document containers such as DOCX or PDF as the canonical storage layer. Importer priority is one-way into local state first, with cloud sync remaining an explicit later user action. Apple Journal, GitJournal, Joplin, Obsidian, Day One, ZIP, JSONL, Git/WebDAV/S3/R2, and local folder flows should all map into or out of this same Markdown/JSON/media archive shape rather than becoming separate sources of truth. The first Apple Journal importer phase is ZIP-only because Flutter web can reliably read one selected archive, while recursive folder reads need a desktop-only dart:io path. Settings -> Developer -> Import Apple Journal ZIP parses Markdown/JSON entries, stores referenced media in LocalAttachmentStore, writes GFM/frontmatter drafts into an existing or new local category, logs each import stage in the Debug log, and leaves cloud sync paused until the user explicitly runs Push local -> cloud. Note URLs use #/notes/<uuid> so the copied link and the browser URL match the viewed note. Public UUID links render read-only when opened cold; private links keep the URL in place and show a sign-in prompt instead of redirecting back to the editor root. Legacy owned categories named Inbox are handled as a user-directed data migration. After a clean signed-in load, the editor offers to move their notes into a new category or remove the old category property so the notes fall into the uncategorized bucket. The backend already preserves notes on category deletion via course_id = NULL, so this flow does not require a schema migration.

626.body: Found while running the real Veronica-7 migration end-to-end against production (step 2 + 3). Import worked perfectly — 193 notes, 6 modules, 0 warnings, idempotent on re-import — but the first sync of the 193-note course 503'd after 120 s , and the fork showed a flood of ~70 partial notechondria: sync … commits before the worker was killed. The push was non-atomic and never completed.
626.breadcrumbs: 0.1.176 - Fix: course sync as ONE atomic commit (Git Data API) » Context
626.title: Context

627.body: courses/git_service._commit_files (0.1.174) wrote each file with a separate Contents API PUT — i.e. one commit per file . For a 193-file course that is ~386 sequential GitHub round-trips inside a single HTTP request: it exceeded the gateway timeout (503 to the client), the worker was terminated mid-loop (partial, non-atomic push, git_pending_since left set with no git_last_sync_error), and it polluted the repo history with hundreds of one-file commits.
627.breadcrumbs: 0.1.176 - Fix: course sync as ONE atomic commit (Git Data API) » Root cause
627.title: Root cause

628.body: _commit_files now pushes all mapped files in one commit via the Git Data API , a fixed handful of calls regardless of file count: GET git/ref/heads/<branch> → base commit sha GET git/commits/<sha> → base tree sha POST git/trees with base_tree + every file as a blob entry (unmanaged files — .vitepress/**, code, CI — stay from the base tree) short-circuit : if the new tree sha equals the base tree sha, the recomposed markdown is byte-identical → return without creating an empty commit POST git/commits (single commit) → PATCH git/refs/heads/<branch> Atomic (all-or-nothing), fast (well within the request timeout), and one clean commit. Structured CourseGitServiceError on any step's failure so sync_course_to_repo records git_last_sync_error and re-raises. Also: git_path is now exposed on NoteDetailSerializer (read-only) so the owner/agent can inspect a git-imported note's repo mapping — it was persisted correctly (proven by idempotent re-import) but invisible over the API.
628.breadcrumbs: 0.1.176 - Fix: course sync as ONE atomic commit (Git Data API) » Fix
628.title: Fix

7.body: Each app paints its local data first and never waits on the backend without a bound: web/index.html shows a static copy of the splash header (no spinner) until Flutter's first frame, and the Flutter splash takes over in the same place, so there is one loading screen (since 0.1.199). The splash names the running step, for example Connecting to server: Planner.Startup/handshake. If the Flutter loader fails to download or throws, or nothing has rendered after 20s, the page shows the cause and a Reload button. Backend requests made during startup, the error banner's Retry, and its Work offline are capped at 10s, and later requests in the same pass fail fast after the first timeout. An unresponsive backend therefore ends in the "Cloud data not loaded: .Startup/bootstrap — the server did not respond within 10s" banner over local data, with Work offline and Retry. A startup step that throws (for example a corrupt local cache) shows a failure screen with Retry and Continue anyway. Uncaught errors before the first frame, and widget build errors, render visible fallbacks instead of a blank page. Every startup step (local data, API base, handshake, session restore, sign-in callback, initial data) writes a <App>.Startup/<step> record to the debug log (Settings > Debug log) with its duration and, on failure, the cause, such as timeout after 10s (server did not respond) or connection refused. Messages, banners, and dialog errors are selectable and have a Copy button (since 0.1.199). The planner imports .ics files on the device when signed out, offline, or when the server is unreachable, and keeps them across reloads (since 0.1.199; see client/planner_app.md ). Subscribing to a calendar URL still needs a cloud session. See the src/startup/ section of client/notechondria_shared.md . The separate version banner compares the build's APP_VERSION with the backend handshake. A newer backend shows "A new version is available. Refresh to update."; an older backend shows "A new version is rolling out". A build without APP_VERSION reports 0.1.21 and shows a false update banner, so every build path passes it (see development/local_dev.md ).

701.body: PlannerEvent gained a recurrence rule stored on the single base row (no per-occurrence materialisation): recurrence_freq — N does-not-repeat (default), W weekly, M monthly, Y yearly. recurrence_interval — every N periods (default 1). recurrence_end_date — inclusive last date the series may occur. recurrence_count — total occurrences including the first. Migration planner/0004_plannerevent_recurrence.py (additive; the four fields all have defaults / are nullable, so it is safe on the live DB). calendar_week_payload (notes/services.py) now expands the series into the requested window: New helpers _add_months (day-clamping, leap-safe), _add_period, _expand_occurrence_dates (honours end-date and count, guarded by a 4000-occurrence ceiling), and _occurrence_payload (shifts starts_at/ends_at by the day delta so the time-of-day is preserved and tags occurrence_date). The grid query now selects one-time events inside the window plus every recurring series (its base may predate the window) and expands each. Recurring series contribute their single next upcoming occurrence (400-day horizon) to the deadlines/urgency list so a weekly class does not flood it. planner_event_payload exposes the four recurrence fields; PlannerEventWriteSerializer accepts them (choice/int/date validation); the list-create and detail-patch views persist them.

711.body: Root causes + fixes: Backend claim. CASDOOR_CLAIM_AVATAR defaulted to avatar only — Casdoor's custom token field, present only when the operator enabled it in the application Token Format. Tokens carry the standard OIDC picture claim by default. Default is now avatar,picture (_claim_str takes the first non-empty), so avatars resolve regardless of token-format config. Backend payload. image_url was avatar_url or local — once a Casdoor avatar_url was set, the locally-uploaded image URL was never sent, so the SPA had no fallback when the Casdoor image failed to load. Both the login/exchange payload and the settings serializer now also expose image_upload_url (the local upload, always); image_url stays the effective avatar for backward compatibility. Frontend fallback (portal). The avatar widget (_RemoteMedia / _RemoteAvatar) now takes a fallback URL: it shows the Casdoor avatar_url first and, when that is empty or fails to load (Casdoor offline / 404), falls back to the local image_upload_url, then the initials placeholder. This realizes "Casdoor when readable, legacy uploader when Casdoor is offline." Older payloads without the new fields fall back to image_url. Editor and planner get the backend fixes immediately (shared); porting the frontend on-error fallback into their avatar widgets is a follow-up (they retain the prior effective-image_url behavior, not a regression).

75.body: Import iCal no longer needs a cloud session or a reachable backend. The file (.ics, or the first .ics inside a .zip) is read and parsed on the device by the shared parseIcalEvents (notechondria_shared/lib/src/utils/ical_events.dart). The review dialog shows the same count that is imported. A file with no readable DTSTART stays in the dialog with an inline, copyable message: Calendar not imported: Planner.Sync.Calendar/parse — "<file>" has no VEVENT entries with a readable DTSTART. Signed in and online, the import is unchanged: POST to /api/v1/calendar-feeds/ (Planner.Sync.Calendar/push). Signed out, in offline mode, or when that upload fails, the calendar is saved on the device instead: Calendar saved on this device: Planner.Sync.Calendar/import — "<title>" (<n> events) is stored locally because <reason>; it is not uploaded to the cloud. After a failed upload, <reason> is the cloud upload failed (<cause>) and the SnackBar is shown as a warning (10s instead of 6s); the dialog still closes because the calendar was imported. Local calendars live in notechondria.planner.local_calendar_feeds (their own bucket, so "Clear cached data" and a signed-in reload keep them). Each record uses the local-archive calendar_feeds.json shape with is_local_feed: true, source_file, and the parsed events (uid, title, description, starts_at, ends_at, all_day). Re-importing a calendar with the same title replaces the earlier local copy. "Clear local data" removes them; .nchron export and restore carry them. Their events appear on the activity week (kind: 'calendar') and in the "Calendar this week" list of the vertical board, which the signed-out view always uses. The offline week now follows week navigation. Limitations: RRULE is not expanded (a recurring event imports its first occurrence), TZID= times are read as device-local time, and local calendars are not uploaded after a later sign-in (tracked in ../TODO.md ). Subscribe by URL stays cloud-only. The server downloads the feed (read_calendar_feed in backend/notes/services.py); a browser cannot fetch another site's .ics cross-origin, and the project does not proxy it. Signed out or offline, the subscribe dialog says so inline: Calendar not subscribed: Planner.Sync.Calendar/subscribe — subscribing by URL needs a cloud session because the server downloads the feed; ... Sign in, or download the .ics file and use Import iCal, which works offline.

797.body: utils/version_status.dart : compareSemver(a, b) (dotted-numeric, pre-release/build suffixes ignored, non-numeric → incomparable), AppVersionStatus { upToDate, updateAvailable, deploying, unsupported }, computeVersionStatus(...), and a BackendVersionInfo carrier. backend version > frontend → updateAvailable (new deploy live, browser still on the cached bundle → refresh) backend version < frontend → deploying (rollout in progress; new bundle served, backend container not flipped yet) frontend < min_frontend_version → unsupported (wins over the version compare) equal / incomparable → upToDate (no banner) components/version_update_banner.dart VersionUpdateBanner: self-contained — owns a periodic probe (default 15 min) + a post-first-frame check, renders a localized top-of-screen banner with a Refresh action (hard browser reload via the web url-strategy), or nothing when current / offline. Soft banners are dismissible; the unsupported one isn't. Returns SizedBox.shrink() otherwise. browserReload() added to the shared web/stub url-strategy. ARB +4 keys (versionUpdateAvailable, versionDeploying, versionUnsupported, versionRefresh).
797.title: Shared (notechondria_shared)

798.body: HandshakeResult gained minFrontendVersion, parsed from the handshake min_frontend_version in each verifyHandshake. A _probeBackendVersion() returns BackendVersionInfo? (null when unreachable) by calling verifyHandshake(apiBaseUrl). VersionUpdateBanner(frontendVersion: _kAppVersion, probe: _probeBackendVersion) is hosted at the top of each app's scaffold body (above the error bar).

799.body: On boot + every 15 min, each app probes the handshake. Offline → nothing (the probe returns null). Designed to also back future mobile update prompts.

870.body: Symptom: a cold-opened share link drops you on the editor home with no note dialog (and not even the private-note prompt) — meaning the fragment was parsed as null. Root cause: the editor uses Flutter's default hash URL strategy (no usePathUrlStrategy()), and the app is a MaterialApp(home:) with no /notes/<uuid> route table. On the first frame Flutter's router normalizes the unmatched initial route and rewrites the hash from #/notes/<uuid> back to #/. The deep-link read (_parseNoteUuidFromUrl → Uri.base.fragment) runs in _bootstrapApp only after await _loadInitialData() (several seconds), by which point the fragment is already gone. The well-tested parseNoteUuidFromFragment regex was never the problem — the fragment was empty by the time it was called. Fix: snapshot the launch fragment in main() into the top-level bootInitialFragment before runApp(), while the URL is still pristine. _parseNoteUuidFromUrl() now reads that snapshot first and only falls back to the (possibly-clobbered) live Uri.base. After the note opens, _replaceNoteUrl(uuid) restores #/notes/<uuid> in the address bar as before. Regression test: editor_app/test/deep_link_open_test.dart — the flutter_test environment has an empty Uri.base.fragment (exactly the clobbered production state), so the test only passes if the boot snapshot drives the deep link. It seeds bootInitialFragment = '/notes/<uuid>', boots with a fake client, and asserts the note viewer opens on the shared note. The existing deep_link_parser_test.dart still covers the pure regex.

896.body: The reaction-simulator splash was dense on small screens and sparse on large ones. Make the particle count scale with screen size, calibrated to the current count (128) for a 1920×1080 screen.

897.body: The particle target is now derived from the viewport area instead of a fixed 128, so on-screen density is constant across screen sizes. notechondria_shared/.../reaction_defs.dart: replaced ReactionSimOptions.maxParticles = 128 with a calibration set — referenceParticles = 128 at referenceArea = 1920×1080, minParticles = 24, maxParticlesCap = 320. reaction_simulator.dart: new ReactionSimulator.targetParticles getter = round(width × height ÷ (referenceArea ÷ referenceParticles)) clamped to minParticles..maxParticlesCap (falls back to 128 before the first setSize). populationTick() now targets this instead of the old constant. The view already calls setSize with the widget constraints, so the field auto-rescales when the window resizes. Calibration points: 1920×1080 → 128; 960×1080 → ~64; a 360×640 phone clamps up to 24 (not left empty); an 8K monitor caps at 320 (not overwhelming).

903.body: A runnable standalone MCP server in cli/ , independent of backend/ (own pyproject.toml, no backend/ imports): notechondria_mcp/config.py — resolves the backend URL + ntc_ API key from env (NOTECHONDRIA_API_URL / NOTECHONDRIA_API_KEY) or ~/.notechondria/config.json; normalizes the /api/v1 suffix; never echoes the key. notechondria_mcp/client.py — a requests-based client sending Authorization: Bearer ntc_<key> on every call (the same auth the in-backend /mcp/ uses — shared credential, one key per user). notechondria_mcp/tools.py — a tool registry mirroring backend/mcp/tools.py names + input schemas, each mapping to a /api/v1/ request. Representative subset: get_profile, notes CRUD (list_notes/get_note/create_note/update_note/ delete_note), list_courses/get_course/create_course, list_events/create_event. notechondria_mcp/server.py — a stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 MCP loop (initialize fetching the user's mcp_skill_md as instructions, tools/list, tools/call, ping, notifications), mirroring backend/mcp/protocol.py. Transport is hand-rolled (no external MCP SDK dependency yet) so the skeleton is self-contained and testable; it can adopt the official Python mcp SDK later without touching the tool layer. notechondria_mcp/__main__.py — notechondria-mcp entry point with check (config + connectivity) and the default serve (stdio). cli/README.md — install, config, agent-host wiring, the parity rule. cli/tests/test_server.py — 10 unit tests (no network, no SDK): registry shape, dispatch, initialize instructions, error codes. No backend change was needed: ntc_ keys already authenticate every /api/v1/ endpoint (ApiKeyAuthentication is in DEFAULT_AUTHENTICATION_CLASSES), and mcp_skill_md is already served by GET /api/v1/settings/.

925.body: Documentation-only. Authored docs/integrations/mcp-cli-migration.md : a phased proposal to move the MCP server out of the Django backend into a standalone CLI app that talks to the backend over the public /api/v1/ surface with the existing Bearer ntc_<key> auth. Highlights: Why: the in-backend /mcp/ tools call the Django ORM directly ( backend/mcp/tools.py ), so MCP can only run where the full backend runs — no distributable/self-hosted story, coupled release cadence, and doc drift. Target: a notechondria-mcp CLI (recommended Python, using the official mcp SDK) whose tool handlers map MCP calls to /api/v1/ requests. Backend stays the source of truth + API + skill.md. Auth unchanged: ntc_ key minted in Settings, pasted into CLI config, sent as Bearer ntc_<key>. Backend changes (additive, non-breaking): expose mcp_skill_md over the API (GET /api/v1/auth/mcp-skill/), audit that /api/v1/ covers every tool operation, confirm CORS, treat /api/v1/ as a stable contract. No DB migration. 5 phases: API gap audit → CLI skeleton → full tool parity → distribute (PyPI) → cutover + delete backend/mcp/. Records open questions for the owner (separate repo vs cli/, Python vs TypeScript, keep /mcp/ hosted or fully cut over) and flags the stale auth-header example in docs/server/mcp.md to fix in Phase 1.

94.body: startup_budget.dart — StartupRequestBudget and runWithStartupBudget. Each app runs its cold start, the load-error banner's Retry, and its Work offline inside a budget. The budget travels as a zone value and HttpClientInternalsMixin.send enforces it: every request is capped at kBackendStartupTimeout (10s), and after the first timeout the rest of the pass fails fast with a BackendStartupTimeout. friendlyError renders that as the localized "did not respond within 10s" message. Requests made after the pass keep their previous unbounded behavior. Known gap: because the budget is a zone value, fire-and-forget work started inside the pass (portal's post-OAuth cloud pull, editor's legacy-Inbox migration) inherits the 10s cap and the fail-fast flag (tracked in ../TODO.md ). Where the fallbacks show up. The backend-unavailable result is the shared LoadErrorBanner over local data, with Work offline and Retry. A startup step that throws shows StartupFailureView (Retry, Continue anyway). Before Flutter paints, each app's web/index.html shows a #nc-boot loading surface (since 0.1.199 a static copy of the splash header with no spinner, so only one loading screen shows); it turns into a failure message with Reload when the bootstrap script fails to download, the loader throws, or no frame appears within 20s. startup_log.dart (0.1.199) — describeRequestFailure(error) turns a failed request or step into a specific cause: timeout after 10s (server did not respond), skipped: an earlier startup request timed out after 10s, connection refused, DNS lookup failed, TLS handshake failed, connection reset before a response, the browser's opaque network error with no readable response (...), HTML instead of JSON (HTTP 502), or the error's first line. It drops URL query strings and redacts Token / Bearer values. StartupOutcome is the (level, message) record a step reports. AppShellLogMixin.startupStep (0.1.199) — each app's core/bootstrap.dart runs every cold-start step through it: local_state, config, handshake, session_restore, oauth_callback, initial_data (source <App>.Startup/<step>). It logs a DEBUG "started" line and the outcome with its duration, or on a throw <consequence>: <App>.Startup/<step> — <cause> before rethrowing, and sets the splash status to '<label>: <App>.Startup/<step>'. The initial_data outcome is a WARNING Startup finished on local data only: ... when the load fell back to local data. Each app's _loadLocalState merges the startup lines with the stored log right after the store load (and _handleBootstrapFailure does it when that load throws), so a failed start still persists its records. The handshake now goes through HttpClientInternalsMixin.send, so it is logged and bounded by the startup budget; its result also answers the version banner's first probe. send logs failures as HTTP request failed: <App>.HTTP/request_failed — GET <host><path> after <n>ms: <cause>., startup requests of 3s or more as <App>.HTTP/slow, and a non-JSON body as Server response not usable: <App>.HTTP/response — expected JSON from ... but received HTML (HTTP <n>, <type>, <n>B) .... Logs never carry tokens, cookies, or profile data. startup_guard.dart — runGuardedApp (used by every main.dart) wraps runApp in runZonedGuarded, chains FlutterError.onError and PlatformDispatcher.instance.onError, and installs StartupErrorWidget as a non-blank ErrorWidget.builder. An uncaught error before the first frame shows StartupFailureApp; later ones are only logged, because the shell's own fallbacks are on screen by then. components/version_update_banner.dart (related, not startup) — VersionUpdateBanner compares the build's APP_VERSION with the handshake version: backend newer shows "A new version is available", backend older shows "rolling out", below min_frontend_version shows "no longer supported". Every build path must pass APP_VERSION, or the 0.1.21 code default triggers a false update banner (see ../development/local_dev.md ).

988.body: New backend/creators/casdoor_password.py: sync_password_from_claims mirrors the JWT-Custom credential claims (password / passwordSalt / passwordType) into User.password — plain via set_password, bcrypt stored as bcrypt$<hash> for Django's BCryptPasswordHasher. Verified live against auth.trance-0.com: current Casdoor scrubs the password claim value (empty string; passwordType = bcrypt), so this path is dormant until the IdP emits the hash. Tracked in docs/TODO.md (watch upstream). password_grant runs Casdoor's ROPC grant (/api/login/oauth/access_token, grant_type=password) and verifies the returned JWT, distinguishing rejected (Casdoor answered no) from unreachable (timeout / 5xx — the outage case). Live-verified with the Alice test account: correct credentials → ok + verified sub; wrong credentials → rejected. LoginSerializer (backend/creators/api.py): when the submitted password fails the local hash, the backend asks Casdoor via password_grant (with one username-variant retry); on success and a sub match against Creator.casdoor_sub, the verified plaintext is stored locally via set_password and login succeeds. Outcome: the current Casdoor password always works on the fallback endpoint while Casdoor is up, and the locally synced hash serves outages. Unlinked legacy accounts never trigger the grant (no auto-bind, consistent with the 0.1.118 link-challenge policy). _sync_creator_from_claims (casdoor_auth.py) additionally calls the claims-based password sync on its existing 5-minute throttle. settings.py: explicit PASSWORD_HASHERS (Django defaults minus Argon2, plus BCryptPasswordHasher), CASDOOR_CLAIM_PASSWORD* claim-name mappings. bcrypt>=4,<5 added to requirements.txt and requirements-render.txt. settings_test.py gained BCryptPasswordHasher so the sync path is testable.

Added docs/development/cross_platform_plan.md : progress snapshot at 0.1.125, prioritized mobile-web findings (F1–F7), tutorials-integration design, phased roadmap (A–D), manual cross-platform test matrix, and the open owner decisions. Root cause identified for the multi-app auth corruption (F1): on GitHub Pages all three apps share one browser origin, and web shared_preferences is origin-scoped — editor / planner / portal use identical storage keys (notechondria.local_*, notechondria.session in each app's lib/core/local_store.dart, plus the unprefixed oauth_* handoff keys in notechondria_shared/lib/src/app_shell/app_shell_oauth_mixin.dart:196-198), so the apps overwrite each other's sessions, settings, drafts, and OAuth intent. Native desktop builds are unaffected, which is why the symptom only appears in browser usage. Fix tracked as the new Urgent TODO item (per-app key namespacing + copy-style migration). Further findings documented: all three web/index.html files lack a viewport meta tag (iPhone Safari renders the desktop breakpoint on a ~980 px virtual viewport); web identity is still the Flutter placeholder ("frontend" / "A new Flutter project." in manifest, title, and apple-mobile-web-app-title); service-worker disabling in frontend-pages.yml means web builds cannot launch offline, and Safari ITP can evict all local data after 7 days of inactivity; oauth_callback in backend/notechondria/api_views.py hardcodes the editor path for all same-tab redirect flows. Updated docs/TODO.md: new "Cross-platform web shell" subsection (Urgent storage-namespacing item, viewport meta, web identity, offline/install decision), new "Tutorials" section (course content + seeding, in-app surfacing), OAuth-callback app routing and Casdoor redirect-URI audit items under Backend / Auth, and rewrote the stale Casdoor migration entry — phases 1–3 landed across 0.1.95–0.1.101, only phases 4–5 remain. Linked the new plan doc from docs/SUMMARY.md and docs/readme.md.
